quotes.race: Download The PricedUp App Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Benvoy takes the proverbial this horse, but we always knew he had plenty of ability - Jo Davis, trainer.

quotes.race: Sodexo Live! Juvenile Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jo [Davis, trainer] got Benvoy and apparently he wasn't a great jumper, but she's got loads of land at her yard and does showjumping, so she's done plenty of work on him. When I rode him the first time at Market Rasen, I didn't think he'd make a racehorse. Don't take it out of context, but I didn't think he'd be like he is today - Gavin Sheehan, jockey.

runners.comment: It wasn't a bad run off 2lb higher here last time; shouldn't be far away
runners.spotlight: Hasn't made any striking progress since winning his maiden in October but it wasn't a bad run off 2lb higher here last time; shouldn't be far away.

stable_tour.quote: He won at 100-1 at Fontwell last month and it wasn't a total surprise to us as his home work was very good - the trainer had a fiver each-way anyway! He'd shown nothing in bumpers as he was pulling too hard then falling down a hole. He's got a mark after his run at Wincanton on Saturday. 12-11-25

runners.comment: Jumping has been an issue in his two runs over fences; novice winner in this sphere
runners.spotlight: Jumping has been an issue in his two runs over fences; lightly raced hurdler with novice honours to his name and worth considering back in this sphere off what's probably a realistic mark; all headgear left off (has always sported either a hood or tongue-tie).

runners.comment: Form dipped in last two races, at Cheltenham then Carlisle where he should have run better
runners.spotlight: Two wins last summer (2m/2m1f, good), the latest off just a 1lb lower mark; form has dipped in his last two races, at Cheltenham and then Carlisle where he should have run better; absent since November.

runners.comment: He's not the easiest to weigh up, but goes handicapping at a modest level here
runners.spotlight: Won his only point by 4l on good ground; beaten 13l and 11l over hurdles so he's not the easiest to weigh up, but goes handicapping at a modest level here.

runners.comment: This might not be quite so demanding as the Exeter race he contested last time
runners.spotlight: Fine on all ground; in a good run of form since the blinkers went on four starts back and this might not be quite so demanding as the Exeter race he contested last time; in the mix.

racecards.verdict: Chasing hasn't worked out for SUN ART and he could be interesting back over hurdles off what looks a manageable mark.

runners.comment: Beaten more than 100l at Chepstow where he raced freely; hood added; limited appeal
runners.spotlight: Beaten more than 100l at Chepstow where he raced freely; hood added; limited appeal.

runners.comment: £32,000 yearling; first foal out of a useful 2m4f-3m1f hurdle/chase winner
runners.spotlight: £32,000 yearling; first foal out of a useful 2m4f-3m1f hurdle/chase winner; tongue-tie fitted for debut and market confidence would be welcomed; yard 1-22 in bumpers this season.

runners.comment: Inexperience was evident but he finished tailed off at Taunton and went off 66-1
runners.spotlight: Inexperience was evident but he finished tailed off at Taunton and went off 66-1.

runners.comment: Too green to do himself justice when beaten 23l at Southwell (soft; 25-1); can improve
runners.spotlight: Too green to do himself justice when beaten 23l at Southwell (soft; 25-1) and entitled to step up on that form.

runners.comment: Hung left-handed in both his races but clearly has the ability to have a major say
runners.spotlight: Short in the betting for both his runs (Southwell, soft; Lingfield, AW), the latest of which was in January; the fact he hung left on both occasions is worrying given the nature of this track, but no doubting his ability to have a major say.

runners.comment: Good form claims on Warwick/Haydock runs and he has the scope to keep improving
runners.spotlight: Similar form at Warwick and Haydock (both good to soft) and was keeping on both times; good form claims and he has the scope to keep improving.

runners.comment: Clear second in an Irish point in January and that form has been franked
runners.spotlight: Clear second in an Irish point in January and the winner has done well this year for Chris Gordon; hood added; possible.

runners.breeder: Ecurie Haras Des Beaux & Mme Martine Bon
runners.comment: Finished midfield but a distance behind the winner when 8-1 at Huntingdon
runners.spotlight: Finished midfield but a distance behind the winner when 8-1 at Huntingdon (good to soft); had to show more.

runners.comment: First foal; dam 11.6f Flat (RPR 84) and 2m/2m1f hurdle winner
runners.spotlight: First foal; dam 11.6f Flat (RPR 84) and 2m/2m1f hurdle winner; trainer doesn't have many bumper runners but she's won one this season.

runners.comment: Friendless in the betting and trailed home last at Stratford in early March (soft)
runners.spotlight: Friendless in the betting and trailed home last at Stratford in early March (soft).

runners.comment: 11-1 when beaten 15l into fourth on soft ground at Catterick in January
runners.spotlight: 11-1 when beaten 15l into fourth on soft ground at Catterick in January; more needed but may encounter drier conditions this time.

runners.comment: Dam 3m1f/3m2f hurdle winner; yard has occasional success in bumpers
runners.spotlight: First foal; dam 3m1f/3m2f hurdle winner, closely related to winners Tarada (2m3f hurdle/3m chase) and Travada (point/bumper and 3m chase); yard has occasional success in bumpers and the market needs checking.

racecards.verdict: This doesn't look a strong bumper. OYKEL BRIDGE and My Mate AJ bring the best form. Alan King's runner gets the nod.

runners.owner: Middleham Park Racing Cxx & M Parker
runners.comment: Largely progressive form includes good performances in two sales races; in the mix
runners.spotlight: Beaten favourite in the Two Year Old Trophy at Redcar when last seen but otherwise a progressive sort and may do better still; performed well in sales races at York (won) and Doncaster (close second; form has been strongly franked); capable of playing a big role, even off top weight.

runners.comment: Ran well in one of his Listed attempts but has to overcome a difficult mark
runners.spotlight: Had an easy task for sole win; good second in sales/Listed races at York, including behind Song Of The Clyde, but form dipped sharply on final 2yo start; has a difficult mark in this first handicap attempt.

runners.comment: Has a bit to prove back at 6f but can't be written off; William Buick prefers Treanmor
runners.spotlight: Absent since coming up short in Listed grade at York Ebor festival when bidding for 5f hat-trick; return to 6f presents a question mark in this competitive field and William Buick prefers Treanmor; however, cost 1,400,000gns at the Craven breeze-up a year ago and can't be written off.

runners.comment: Impressive over C&D last May and looks interesting back in this scenario on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Cost 2,000,000euros as a yearling and impressively justified favouritism over C&D (good to firm) last May on debut; beaten in three races over 7f/1m since but ran well at Meydan latest; gelded since; interesting with progress possible returned to this scenario on handicap debut.

quotes.race: Enter ITV7 For Free Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were hopeful it was going to be straightforward, Treanmor is a straightforward horse to deal with and shows a lot of class. We've been lucky that the two-year-olds have been running well so we had a bit of a gauge on him. We've never taken him off the bridle at home so I said to William to be wary of that if he had to ask the question. There should be an abundance of improvement to come. We had pencilled in a plan for the Chesham but he hasn't lacked pace there so we'll see - Charlie Appleby, trainer, speaking on ITV.

runners.comment: Tad exposed, as record of 0-6 since debut success reflects; below par last time
runners.spotlight: Good seventh of 19 at the York Ebor festival (6f) in sole handicap attempt but is a tad exposed, as record of 0-6 since debut success reflects; below-par third of four in conditions race on final 2yo start.

quotes.race: Frank Whittle Partnership ebfstallions.com Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: First Legion had breezed very well and was bought with a big reputation. He was a little bit keen in the middle of the race, but he picked up good. He came from a good breeze-up place and he'll improve on good, fast ground - Shane Foley, rider.

runners.comment: Returns to turf; chance largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear
runners.spotlight: Reasonably exposed and doesn't look the answer on the balance of his AW form this year; gained his 2yo wins at a lower level; chance largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear.

quotes.race: British Stallions Studs EBF Nursery Handicap (A Hamilton Park 2-Y-O Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Rogue Supremacy obviously carried a lot of weight and, being odds-on, I'd have liked to see him win by further. But Danny [Tudhope, jockey] said the further he was going, the better he was travelling and maybe could have pressed the button a bit earlier - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.race: Eat In The White Rose Bistro Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Very straightforward. Rogue Supremacy jumped well but there was no real pace on early. I would have been happy to get a lead but he ends up in front and we went fairly steady fractions early on and he was in cruise control after that. He's a horse we like a lot at home and it's a good start - Danny Tudhope, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Commenced last season with two wins; this reappearance may be the time to catch him
runners.spotlight: Absent and gelded since disappointing in Ayr nursery in September when back down in class after defeats at Listed/Group level; commenced last season with two wins over 6f, looking a useful sort, and this reappearance may be the time to catch him; remains of interest.

quotes.race: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Reciprocated is turning out to be a really nice horse. We'll definitely look at stakes races now. He had a penalty and he did it really easily. He's got plenty of size and scope about him, he'll improve again for that run and the further he goes, the better he'll get - James Cowley, assistant to Karl Burke.

runners.comment: Ex-Irish; 1-1 at handicap level but this looks a stiffer task on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Scored twice during his spell with Ger Lyons, then posted duck eggs in two Listed events for Charles Byrnes; gelded since; 1-1 at handicap level but this looks a tougher task on debut for new stable.

quotes.race: Harvertech Maiden
quotes.quote: Like ours do from their first time out, Sir Alfie has come on an awful lot. You do need a run here for experience because it is a trappy 5f. Leigh said that when the other horse got to him, he put his head down like a terrier and fought back and then he couldn't pull him up so there is an extra furlong up his sleeve - Shane Lyons, assistant trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Raised 4lb for finishing fifth in substandard AW Group 3 but may do better still
runners.spotlight: Gained her handicap success at a major track (6f) but against only three rivals and faces a tougher scenario in this deeper field; 4lb rise for final effort (fifth in substandard AW Group 3) adds to the difficulty; on a positive note, there is a chance she can still improve further.

runners.comment: 11lb rise in his mark in this ongoing bid for a first turf win; 2-2 on AW
runners.spotlight: Appeared to run well in valuable prize at York (7f) on final 2yo start but an 11lb rise in his mark doesn't help in this ongoing bid for a first turf success; 2-2 on AW, both performances at Newcastle (6f/7f).

quotes.race: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: I planned to get a lead but Advertised is very genuine and straightforward and I thought if I could get an easy lead, I know he's got a good turn of foot and I just turned it into a sprint from the three [furlong pole] - Oliver Stammers, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse. We got him beat on his debut by running him over 5f. The winner, who's gone in again, was from the breeze-ups and just caught him out. He won at Newcastle when he hit the front and pricked his ears - he's a very laid-back character. He looked like he wanted seven and he might, but I think a stiff six is going to be great for him. He shows more speed at home than he does at the track and I think there's a lot more to come. He has a sales race entry at the Curragh on September 14 and that's his target. He'd probably have 10lb to find there but I think he can be competitive. 04-09-25

runners.breeder: Attlehill Ltd T/A Ridge Manor Stud
runners.comment: Completed a September double; looks open to further progress this term; possibilities
runners.spotlight: Built on debut effort by completing a September double, showing versatility with the wins over 6f on fast ground and 5f on soft; readily defied a penalty in novice event at Beverley and looks open to further progress this season; possibilities.

quotes.race: Free Tips Daily On attheraces.com EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ironwill battled hard, especially as he's a big horse, but Marco managed to get him to settle nicely. He's got the ability to improve a bit - Stuart Williams, trainer.

runners.comment: Brings good stats, being 3-6 overall, 2-2 in handicaps and 2-2 over 6f; one to consider
runners.spotlight: Brings very good stats, being 3-6 overall, 2-2 in handicaps (both Class 4) and 2-2 over 6f; prevailed narrowly at Newbury (soft) on last appearance; now 2lb higher in a better race but may have further improvement in her; one to consider.

quotes.race: Hazell & Jefferies Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a hugely gutsy performance off topweight. We thought Lebron Power lacked the stamina for six furlongs but she did it through grit and determination - Sean Levey, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Newcomers' Maiden Stakes (Horses Which Have Never Run) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lebron Power found the ground a little bit quick but she's sharp, she's genuine and she's straightforward. She picked up nicely and hopefully she keeps on improving - Sean Levey, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Proved unable to take record to 3-3 and RPRs suggests he's on a stiff mark
runners.spotlight: Absent since finishing last of four in Salisbury conditions race when attempting to take record to 3-3; may still have more to offer but RPRs suggest he's facing a stiff task off a mark of 87 in this deep field.

runners.comment: Gained reappearance win in AW maiden that threw up the winner of this contest last year
runners.spotlight: Made all for comfortable reappearance success in Wolverhampton maiden (6f, AW) that was won last year by Double Rush, who followed up in this race; mark is unaltered for this second attempt at handicap level; interesting given his good credentials and likelihood of further progress.

runners.comment: Looks the type to improve further and do well in handicaps for her major connections
runners.spotlight: Made all in Wolverhampton maiden (7f, AW) to take her 2yo record to 321; likely to be as effective back down in distance; looks the type to improve further and do well in handicaps for her major connections; attractively weighted near the bottom of the card and is one for the shortlist.

runners.comment: Needed a switch to AW to open his account; goes into deeper waters back on turf
runners.spotlight: Required a switch to AW at Wolverhampton (6f maiden) to open his account at the fourth attempt, and needs further improvement to follow up in this warm handicap back on turf; wears first-time headgear.

racecards.verdict: The signs look good for SOVEREIGN SPELL (nap) who is a very similar type to last year's winner. Reciprocated is second pick.

racecards.race_name: Betway Wood Ditton Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 120,000gns yearling by Ghaiyyath; market may help ahead of this introduction
runners.spotlight: 120,000gns yearling by Ghaiyyath; sixth foal; half-brother to winners Warnie (6f-1m including 2yo/Australian Group 2; RPR 115), Montpellier Green (7f 2yo; 81) and Mutaraafeq (1m AW; 79); dam French 9.7f AW winner (including 2yo), half-sister to 1m1f Listed winner On Call Now; respected connections and market may help ahead of this introduction.

runners.comment: 34,000euros foal, 25,000gns yearling; best watched unless the betting suggests otherwise
runners.spotlight: By Ghaiyyath; 34,000euros foal, 25,000gns yearling; second foal; half-brother to German 1m2f winner Poyraz Approach; dam unraced sister to useful winners News At Six (1m2f-1m4f) and Leafy Shade (6f 2yo/8.5f); likely best watched on this first go unless the betting suggests otherwise.

runners.comment: Already-gelded son of Lope De Vega; powerful connections and he's a key contender
runners.spotlight: Already-gelded son of Lope De Vega; third foal; half-brother to 5f winner Mc Loven (including 2yo/AW; RPR 88); dam 6f 2yo winner (81), half-sister to winners Blair House (UAE 1m1f Group 1) and Key Victory (1m2f Listed), out of maiden sister to 1m Group 1 winner Poet's Voice; represents powerful connections who have fielded winners of this race before; key contender.

runners.breeder: Ecurie Des Monceaux, Forz Europe Ltd & M
runners.comment: 50,000euros yearling; mixed messages distance-wise from this gelding's pedigree
runners.spotlight: 50,000euros yearling by Dark Angel; fourth foal; half-brother to German 1m1f AW winner Bavaria; dam 9.4f-1m4f winner (including AW/Listed; RPR 102), sister to unraced dam of 6f Group 1 winner Shaquille, out of 5f Group 2 winner; mixed messages distance-wise from this gelding's pedigree but he's worth a market check.

runners.owner: Hasmonean Racing, S Hope & S Barrow
runners.comment: By Palace Pier; yard in decent nick but gelding's claims would be aided by market support
runners.spotlight: By Palace Pier; tenth foal; closely related to 1m-1m4f winner Mashhoor (including Group 3; RPR 115), half-brother to seven winners including Fambrus (Italian 1m7f Listed; 101) and Faciascura (Italian 1m2f Group 3; 100); dam Italian Group-placed 1m2f/1m3f winner; yard in decent nick but this gelding's claims would be aided by market support.

runners.comment: 390,000euros yearling by New Bay; leading yard won this with well-backed colt last year
runners.spotlight: 390,000euros yearling by New Bay; third foal; half-brother to 1m AW winner Indian Spirit (RPR 86); dam Listed-placed 1m2f winner (96), half-sister to winners Sabbeeh (smart 6f-1m) and Dream Day (useful 6f 2yo), out of 7f Listed winner/1,000 Guineas fourth; the most expensive of these at auction and hails from a leading yard that won this with a well-backed colt last year; betting should prove informative again.

runners.owner: HM The King & HM The Queen
runners.comment: By Frankel out of French 1,000 Guineas winner; of obvious interest with Ryan Moore booked
runners.spotlight: By Frankel; second foal; half-brother to 1m winner Crown Estate (including AW; RPR 100); dam 1m winner (including AW and French 1,000 Guineas; 112), half-sister to 7f Listed winner Top Score, out of unraced sister to this yard's top-class 7f-1m2f winner Raven's Pass; plenty of blue blood in that pedigree and he's one of two for a stable that won this in 2021 and 2022; of obvious interest on this debut with Ryan Moore booked.

runners.comment: By Dubawi out of a French Oaks winner; must be considered with Oisin Murphy on board
runners.spotlight: Dubawi fifth foal; brother to winners Lord Of Love (1m2f/1m4f; RPR 102) and Governor Of India (1m2f AW; 77); dam 1m-10.5f winner (including 2yo/French Oaks; 109), closely related to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner English Ballet, half-sister to 1m Listed winner King Of Comedy; lots to like about that pedigree and it will be interesting to see what the market makes of him, particularly in relation to his top stable's other contender Portcullis; firmly considered with Oisin Murphy up.

runners.comment: 65,000gns yearling by Kingman; holds a Derby entry; look for market support
runners.spotlight: 65,000gns yearling by Kingman; second foal; half-brother to 1m2f AW winner Star Cast (RPR 71); dam Listed-placed 7f/1m winner (including 2yo/AW; 105), is granddaughter of 11.7f winning sister to 7f Group 3 winner Yalaitanee; the only one of these to hold a big-race entry (The Derby) so look for market support to back that up.

runners.comment: The sole filly and she's best watched without good market support
runners.spotlight: Dream Ahead sixth foal; half-sister to four winners including Ventura Gold (7f-1m1f including AW; RPR 79), Chloe's Courage (7f AW; 56) and Kannon (French 5.5f/7.5f); dam 7f AW winner (76), out of 11.7f winning sister to 7f Group 3 winner Yalaitanee; the sole filly and best watched without good market support.

racecards.verdict: The betting will be a key piece of the Wood Ditton puzzle but the suggestion is PORTCULLIS ahead of stablemate Santushti.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Crown Knott, 9/4 Portcullis, 3/1 Santushti, 6/1 North Beach, 14/1 Bemersyde, 33/1 Impierious,  Take A Chill Pill, 50/1 Dark Whisper, 66/1 Cosmo Brown, 100/1 Me An' All

runners.comment: Steadily progressive; won by 1l going away from Jasour at Doncaster on seasonal debut
runners.spotlight: Steadily progressive, mostly in handicaps, throughout his career; won by 1l going away from Jasour in Listed event at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) on seasonal debut, looking better than ever and taking record to 6-23; solid second in both C&D starts; enters calculations upped further in grade.

quotes.race: William Hill Price Boosts Every Day Cammidge Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Aramram worked at Kempton on Monday and worked super. Sean [Levey, jockey] kind of made me run him, I wanted to go down the handicap route. He has improved from last year, that's very clear and I'm delighted. He's ultra-consistent, he's very talented and his commitment is faultless - Richard Hannon, trainer.

quotes.race: BetMGM Handicap
quotes.quote: I was positive enough on Aramram and the leader was towing him along really nicely, but a couple others just started to move and I flinched on him, and he picked up a lot quicker than I thought he would. He ended up being in front a big long but he was brave once he realised the horse on his far side started to give him a race, and knuckled back down. He's a lovely, genuine horse and he's been super competitive in some hard races - Tom Marquand, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I'm delighted with the way he's been running, and although he's due to go up another 3lb for finishing second again, which I think is slightly unfair. He's still a very nice horse for races like the Wokingham and the Stewards' Cup. 22-04-25

runners.comment: Dead-heated with Diligent Harry in Listed race, taking AW record to 4-8; just 1-9 on turf
runners.spotlight: Dead-heated with Diligent Harry in Listed grade to complete a Lingfield 6f double in January and take AW record to 4-8; effective when fresh but is by no means certain to transfer the improvement back to turf; only 1-9 in this sphere; tongue-tie applied.

quotes.race: Midnite Kachy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Ideally Ryan would have wanted to come on the outside, but he was forced to go inside. He's a good jockey and got the job done. There isn't anything suitable for Completely Random on the all-weather after this, so we'll probably wait for the turf season - Harry Charlton, trainer.

quotes.race: Wokingham Stakes (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Completely Random got a little bit far back and had to work his way through them, flew at the line and looks a nice type to win one of these races at some point. I like the idea of the Stewards' Cup - Harry Charlton, trainer.

quotes.race: Carling King Richard III Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: We're delighted with that. Completely Random is very progressive, straightforward and is effective over five or six furlongs. We had this race in mind for him after he won at Southwell and the plan is to prepare him for the Wokingham at Royal Ascot - Harry Charlton, trainer.

runners.comment: Posted peak RPR on turf but needs an even bigger effort to gain first win in this sphere
runners.spotlight: Record of 0-5 on turf compared to 2-3 on AW; admittedly registered his peak RPR in this sphere when second Elmonjed in York Listed contest (6f) on penultimate appearance; however, needs an even bigger effort to go one better in this field.

quotes.race: Thorley Taverns Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Crestofdistinction has built well over the winter and he's always shown a lot of ability at home. He's had two racecourse gallops at Kempton prior to this and shaped up well from each one. We put the cheekpieces on because he's such a laidback horse and he's got the potential to keep improving into a nice sprinter. He's going the right way about things and I always thought he was quite smart. He was quite green last year but it was a much different story today, he pretty much dominated as soon as he jumped out - David Probert, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He was third and second on his two starts last year at Doncaster and Kempton and we decided to give him a little bit of a break. He had a setback at the start of last year, which knocked his summer out, but he's back in full training and doing well. He should be able to go and win his maiden and then go on to bigger and better things. He could really progress through the sprints and handicap division this year. 02-04-25

runners.comment: Good strike-rate on AW includes a Lingfield Listed double this year; 0-18 on turf
runners.spotlight: Good strike-rate on AW includes a Listed sprint double at Lingfield this year, sharing the spoils with Completely Random on reappearance; similar to that rival, looks far from guaranteed to maintain the form back on turf; 0-18 in this sphere.

quotes.race: Midnite Hever Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Diligent Harry is a grand old boy and they went a good gallop. I was able to jump and get him into a rhythm. I struggled to pull him up after the line. He seemed to have taken a step forward from last time and he's versatile as five or six furlongs is fine for him - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

quotes.race: JenningsBet Chipchase Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: If anything I was getting a little bit lonely in front from the furlong pole. Watching Diligent Harry's replays, when one comes to him he really sticks his head down. This horse has a lot of class. He was third in a Group 1 last year. I've ridden him out the last couple of weeks and Clive [Cox, trainer] was extremely positive on his chances. He said he's got a big one in him - Saffie Osborne, jockey.

quotes.race: 1895 Duke Of York Clipper Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: We did our fight there, then the first and second came at us late in the day. I'm very proud of Diligent Harry, it was a big run. I'm very pleased and he's in a good place. I couldn't be more happier bar winning. We've got him in the King Charles III at Royal Ascot as a stiff five furlongs is more in our favour - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.race: BetUK Hever Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: We were worried about the drop back to the minimum [trip], but Clive thought there would be plenty of pace on which would suit Diligent Harry and he was right. There are plenty of options going forward after that - Martin Bosley, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: BetUK All-Weather Sprint Championships Conditions Stakes
quotes.quote: It was a great ride. I'm looking forward to the summer with Diligent Harry, he's exciting. He's got a bit of confidence, gelding has helped him and he's matured - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes 3 Year Old All-Weather Championships Conditions Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: We're a little bit away from that [Commonwealth Cup] at the moment but let's hope Diligent Harry takes a step forward. I still think he could be quite special - Adam Kirby, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Unibet New Instant Roulette Novice Stakes
quotes.quote: Diligent Harry is still a bit of a baby but he has some size about him and he should be a nice horse for the turf this summer - Clive Cox, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well last week at Southwell when third under top weight, which was his best run of the year, and he now runs on All-Weather Championships finals day at Newcastle on Friday. He won at the meeting two years ago and I'm looking forward to running him. 17-04-25

It was great to see him back to near his best when second in the Group 3 Hackwood Stakes at Newbury. He had enjoyed a good campaign before that, having won twice at Newcastle, the latter being the All-Weather Sprint Championships. The form of that race is pretty hot as the runner-up, Witch Hunter, went on to win at Royal Ascot, while further down the field Vadream has gone on to win the Group 3 Palace House Stakes at Newmarket. He has yet to win on grass, but his head second to Commanche Falls last time, one of the most consistent horses in training, shows that there are big races to be won with him. I think the Hopeful Stakes at Newmarket is a possible logical step after that fine effort. At some point we will give him a break before preparing him for the next all-weather season. 02-08-23

runners.comment: Recorded last three wins at York and may be more interesting when back there
runners.spotlight: Has form on the Newmarket tracks but recorded last three wins at York, including when beating Crestofdistinction with more in hand than the narrow margin suggests in Listed grade on most recent appearance; likely to be more interesting when back at that venue.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Dash Handicap
quotes.quote: Jim [Crowley, jockey] said 'run him on Saturday, I would!' We'll see. It's a different sort of track but Elmonjed likes a big field and being covered up and helped through. He's not really happy being on his own in front as long as he was today but he hung on. He'd be better on faster ground too - Maureen Haggas, trainer's wife

quotes.race: Sky Bet Constantine Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: The horse is tough since he's had the headgear put on him. Elmonjed was idling without it and needed it to make him concentrate. He hits flat spots in his races and it wouldn't amaze me if he got further one day. It's very much one step at a time with him, but he could be good enough for a bigger prize in time - Angus Gold, racing manager to Shadwell Estates.

quotes.race: AC Plastics Limited EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: It looked like the runner-up had got away from him a bit so Elmonjed did well to win under a penalty and I really liked how he put his head down in the final furlong. He surprised us a little at Lingfield and has really improved from his debut. He was gelded in the summer because he was misbehaving but he's a good-looking horse and progressing with time. He's entered at Chantilly next Saturday and that's a pretty quick turnaround, but we'll talk with Sheikha Hissa and William [Haggas] and make a plan. He's going in the right direction and is a really nice horse - Richard Hills, assistant racing manager for owners Shadwell.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Shadwell have another nice horse on their hands. Elmonjed has done well to overcome that greeness early on what is a sharp track - Tom Marquand, jockey speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Very useful and has Group 1 form; solid effort behind Aramram at Doncaster on reappearance
runners.spotlight: Very useful 6f performer who registered last success in Group 3 contest at Ascot two years ago; has Group 1 form, including creditable sixth in the 2025 July Cup; made a solid start to his 2026 campaign with 1l second to Aramram at Doncaster; again likely to be thereabouts.

quotes.race: Commonwealth Cup (Group 1) (British Champions Series) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: That was a great run. I'm very pleased. Obviously the winner was impressive. Jasour just switched leads right before the line, which might have cost us second, but he's run a blinder. I'm thrilled he's going the right way. I think we are close enough to warrant a kick at the July Cup, a race in which three-year-olds have done really well in the past. That would be my first thoughts as they cross the line, and as long as he comes back ok from here, he's a horse who deserves to be in the top flight - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.race: Commonwealth Cup Trial Stakes (Group 3) (Registered As The Pavilion Stakes)
quotes.quote: Jasour was class last year in the July Stakes, then in the Morny they split and he was in the middle and just went too free. I think he got a little bit frightened as a juvenile, so we've worked and worked and he had some precious turnout up until Christmas at home. The whole team has worked really hard to be sure that we've kept him right and Jim [Crowley, jockey] seemed to really strike a chord with him in the July Stakes, so I'm just pleased the whole plan has come off. I was a little worried the ground would be too easy for him, but that didn't seem to be a problem. The Commonwealth Cup is absolutely the plan, and the Sandy Lane would be nice. We're looking forward to seeing him on a better surface and Jim has given him a super confidence-building ride. Winning was a super bonus I wasn't entirely sure would happen - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.race: Kingdom Of Bahrain July Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: It's the first time I'd ridden Jasour but riding him from off the pace has been the key to him - Jim Crowley, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's won at the track and was third in last year's Commonwealth Cup. He was only sixth on his reappearance at Haydock but he didn't have a great lead-up with a bruised foot and he was a little bit fresh, so I'd hope he can take a big step forward from that. 10-06-25

Right from day one he looked a little bit special. His homework suggested he was good enough to win on his debut, but he was a little unlucky there as he went down by a neck having jumped the road at Salisbury. He won next time out at Nottingham, again over 5f, but I thought he was crying out for an extra furlong on that occasion. He could have gone to Royal Ascot but he just wasn't ready. He progressed from his win to his third run in the July Stakes at Newmarket. I was positive about his chances there and he duly obliged, running out an impressive winner. We now have to decide which route to take. I am not one to waste my owner's money on lots of fancy entries, so you can tell how much I thought of him as I had given him an entry in the Gimcrack before he ran at Newmarket. But if he went to the Gimcrack he probably could not go for the Group 1 Prix Morny which is just over a week later, but if he goes to the Richmond at Goodwood on Thursday there would be the ideal time between races. So, at the moment I'm leaning towards Glorious Goodwood, but we will see how the horse is before finalising plans. 02-08-23

runners.comment: Group winner in Ireland; seemed to need the run at Doncaster on debut for new yard
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish gelding whose good spell in 2024 featured a Group 3 win and who ran creditably a few times last year; seemed to need the run at Doncaster on stable/seasonal debut but has work to do to reverse placings with Aramram and Jasour.

quotes.race: SBK Renaissance Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: My Mate Alfie has improved all season. We've been teaching him to sprint all year and he got what he deserved today. He is just very straightforward and we might go touring with him next year - Ger Lyons, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Bold Lad Sprint Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: My Mate Alfie is one of those fantastic horses. He has such a good heart. He is going to mature into a better horse next year so fingers crossed - Ger Lyons, trainer.

quotes.race: Jebel Ali Racecourse & Stables Dash Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: My Mate Alfie has been very consistent all year The blinkers have transformed him. The first furlong had me worried, I thought it was going to develop into a real sprint. He's in the Stewards Cup, I was fourth in the race a few years ago. It's massive prize money and if you're serious about that, you have to take part - Ger Lyons, trainer.

runners.comment: Has form figures of 12113 on good/firmer; interesting provided he gets similar ground
runners.spotlight: Only fifth when favourite for AW event on reappearance but is reasonably interesting back on turf, provided he gets ideal ground; has form figures of 12113 on good/firmer, the final effort in Listed grade behind Elmonjed; may still have more to offer.

quotes.race: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I think Prince Of India is ready to step up in class and once he gets some more give in the ground he'll appreciate that too. I think he's fast enough for this distance and as he gets stronger he will develop into a real sprinter. I do think there's more to come - Marco Botti, trainer.

runners.comment: Very useful front-runner; unbeaten (4-4) on the Newmarket courses; should make a bold bid
runners.spotlight: Very useful front-runner whose strike-rate is 12-32; bagged Group 3 honours at York (7f) last June and a valuable pot at Doha (6f) most recently; unbeaten (4-4) in 6f contests on the Newmarket courses and has shown that he can win in sizeable fields; likely to make a bold bid back here.

quotes.race: Dukhan Sprint Cup (Local Group 3) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Quinault is an absolute superstar. He's got an amazing will to win and if it's close, he just wants it - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Criterion Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Quinault is a fast horse and on his dam's side, he's definitely bred to go a bit further. Tom [Morley, joint-owner] continually have this argument whether he's best over a stiff six furlongs or an easy seven, but I think it's probably either. He's just a high-class horse who loves to win. Once he gets in front and rolling along at a place like this, he's hard to catch. We'd like to come back here to the Ebor meeting in August as it was a win and you're in race for it. We'll aim for that and be working back from there. He tries very hard and that's the key to it. It's his first Group win and it means a lot. I took him to Dubai in the winter and ran him in a Group 1, as we've always thought he was capable of this sort of thing - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Starman At Tally Ho Stud Garrowby Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: We thought Quinault wouldn't like this ground but he just wants to win - he definitely tries. He's a special horse for a yard the size of ours, especially as he came a long way in such a short space of time last year. He had a little wobble earlier this year and was a little bit ill after we gave him the flu jab, but he's bang in form now. He's such a special horse. There's a chance he improves again next year and I still think he might be better over seven furlongs, so we've got to explore that avenue as well. He'll have a little bit of a break now as he's done his bit for the summer, but we could travel with him. He's a gelding so we'll go where the best prize-money is that he can win. There isn't much point in running him in Group races just for the sake of it - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Jenningsbet Hopeful Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I don't think Quinault was in love with the ground but he just tries very hard - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Liverpool Airport Faster, Easier, Friendlier Queensferry Stakes (Listed)
quotes.quote: I'd love Quinault to go seven furlongs round a bend somewhere if I could find the right race for him - I think that would be ideal. We wouldn't be against travelling him later in the year. We might go abroad somewhere, some of the tighter tracks, maybe in America, somewhere like that might suit him - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: What a special horse Quinault has been for everybody this year. He didn't run a bad race the last day but he's back on song today - it's a special day. He's got one way of running in that you let him stride on in front, and he's so genuine he keeps finding for you - Luke Catton, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: We had Sendintank who won ten handicaps in a season, including four in a week twice, but that was at a much lower level than this - this is very different. Quinault is a very tough horse and he's got loads of talent as well. Luke Catton has done a fantastic job settling him and it's such a shame he cannot do the weight. The horse was just a runaway when he arrived, he would just bolt. We trained him on a treadmill for the first two months so he never left the yard, before we slowly started to introduce him to the Heath, so there's a lot of work gone into what you're seeing today. He's always had the talent, it's just been a case of letting the horse know it and letting him use it - he's always been fast, that wasn't the problem! He's bred to get further so as long as we can keep him settled in his races that's a route we'll look to go with him - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Oakmere Homes Supporting Macmillan Sprint Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: This was the biggest occasion Quinault has been to and he got a little bit warm in the preliminaries but he settled nicely in the race and Connor gave him a lovely ride, just managing to get him there on the line. We put him in at Ascot just in case something happened that forced our hand, but my gut feeling is probably not to run. I think he'll get a bit further and I've put him in the Bunbury Cup so that's a possibility - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Aspall Suffolk Draught Cyder Handicap
quotes.quote: It was unfortunate Luke Catton couldn't ride Quinault today as he couldn't do the weight. Luke has done a brilliant job settling him at home as he was a tearaway when he came but that is why Godolphin put him in the sale in the first place. He will probably go to York now for the valuable three-year-old six-furlong handicap as long as he comes out of this fine - Stuart Williams, trainer.

runners.comment: Capable of smart form but seems unlikely to break his Abernant duck at the fourth attempt
runners.spotlight: Capable of smart form, such as placed efforts in two July Cups, but is getting long in the tooth and seems unlikely to break his Abernant duck at the fourth attempt (record in this race reads 404); losing spell goes back almost three years.

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: Run To Freedom is an amazing horse. When he's absolutely on-song he's a really good horse and he loves a bit of an uphill finish. He's got some fantastic form in Group 1 races, it would be lovely if we could just nick one somewhere. He doesn't like firm ground but he's coping with it now he's older. Firm ground and the draw didn't help him greatly at Ascot but he still finished a neck behind Inisherin, so I don't think he really deserved to be that price. You can never write him off but you could never tip him - Henry Candy, trainer.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network July Cup Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: Run To Freedom is a very able horse and we knew he could do that, he showed it at Salisbury and when second behind Kinross in the Champions Sprint last year. You can never quite rely on him, which is why he starts at these ridiculous prices, but the ability is there. I wouldn't be surprised if he was able to win one before the end of the year. We'll go to Haydock and we'll go to Ascot in October - Henry Candy, trainer.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Asset Finance Handicap
quotes.quote: Hopefully getting his head back in front will spark a revival in Run To Freedom, who looked like he was going to be a world beater as a two-year-old - Henry Candy, trainer.

runners.comment: 5f Listed winner in 2025; produced peak RPR when landing this prize in 2024; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Campaigned mostly over 5f last year, bagging Listed honours at York in July prior to facing stiffer tasks returned to Group 1 level; effective at 6f in the past and produced his peak RPR when landing this prize (on good ground) in 2024; not ruled out.

quotes.race: Connaught Access Flooring Abernant Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We were looking forward to running Washington Heights today and he is a horse that tries very, very hard in his races. He has run loads of good races for us and probably just been a bit unlucky here and there. He had done well over the winter and we were really looking forward to this year. He was impressive when he won in Sweden last year and we were hoping he'd outrun his odds today. Tom has given him a great ride from the front and got the job done. Kevin is a fantastic trainer of fast horses and it looks like he's bought another nice one for us. He's in the Duke of York and Greenlands in Ireland and we could look at Royal Ascot further down the line. We will see what the boss says - Cosmo Charlton, racing manager for owners Hambleton Racing.

quotes.race: Bro Park Sprint Championship (Listed Race) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: All fairness goes to Simon Turner, who runs Hambleton Racing. They've supported this meeting and had success out here before. He came up with the idea and thankfully it's paid off. Washington Heights is so tough and genuine, he deserved to win one like that. He's been a bit unfortunate this year. He bumped into Shaquille at the start of the year and you've seen what he's gone on to do. He's had his day in the sun today. Thankfully we had a few owners out here as well who enjoyed it. He's been at the top table in these handicaps all year, so I'm sure there's more races in him - Adam Ryan, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: Scaleby Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a lovely run at Wetherby and Washington Heights has improved for it as he's quite laid back at home and he's obviously going to come on a lot for that fitness wise too, so we were hoping today that he was going to run a big race again - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a shade unlucky at York as the ground just went against him. If it had been a bit faster, he'd have taken some pegging back. His win in the Abernant proved he was up to Group class and that last run teed him up nicely for the big sprints. 10-06-24

runners.owner: D Bevan And Mrs D Bevan
runners.comment: Won last year's Commonwealth Cup; subsequent defeats can be excused; leading contender
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage filly who held on by a neck in last year's Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm); had excuses for her subsequent defeats in other major sprints at Goodwood (drop back to 5f; still ran creditably) and Haydock (poorly drawn); has the best chance at the weights.

quotes.race: Commonwealth Cup (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: It was very smooth in that we'd planned to follow the American horse [Shisospicy]. Prior to today the draw was a concern but with the first race winner coming from a low draw it gave us the confidence to stay with our plan; we didn't have much choice anyway. Time For Sandals had just been training very well and a good strong pace to aim at was what she needed and Richard [Kingscote] gave her a fantastic ride - Harry Eustace, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Lowther Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted, it was a bit of a leap into the unknown. Time For Sandals travelled very sweetly and lack of experience probably cost her. We may have to look at black type races - Harry Eustace, trainer.

runners.comment: Gelded prior to Cornwallis win, taking record on the Newmarket tracks to 3-3; respected
runners.spotlight: Gelded prior to prevailing narrowly in the Cornwallis (5f, good; Group 3) on final 2yo start, taking record on the Newmarket tracks to 3-3; effective over 6f and looks open to further improvement; carries 3lb penalty; respected kept to this venue in first attempt against his elders.

quotes.race: Newmarket Academy Godolphin Beacon Project Cornwallis Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Full credit to Tara Murphy who rides Beckford's Folly out and has done since day one. He has been a challenge - he has to be stabled and turned most of the day. He started his career as a full horse. He got beat first time and then won his next two starts at Newmarket. We went to the Sirenia [at Kempton] thinking it would be the right sort of race for him but to be fair Oisin [Murphy] rode him that day and he was a challenge from start to finish. He came out of that race even more of a challenge to be honest. So, needless to say, after that we went to geld him and since then he has done very well. Mentally, it has just taken the steam out of him. He put in a good couple of pieces of work since he was gelded. He put in a good piece of work midweek and there was nothing that could take him off the bridle. Once they jumped out today and were going the clip they were, I could see he was hanging on to their coat tails, and I knew he will finish. Full credit to William and the horse - they got the job done. He might come out to Dubai. He is still a challenge even though he is gelded. He wouldn't be a Breeders' Cup horse or anything like that. The reason he comes to Newmarket is that it is less challenging for him and that is why you see his best performances at Newmarket. If we are lucky enough to be looking at him next year as a potential July Cup horse, at least we know it's only up the road! - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Racecourse Syndicates Association Promoting Shared Ownership EBF Confined Novice (Max 1 Run) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We thought Beckford's Folly may need seven furlongs but William got off and said stick to six for now. We were hopeful of a decent show as he got stuck out in the middle of the track at Lingfield on his debut and we took the hood off him this time - Alex Merriam, assistant to trainer Charlie Appleby.

runners.comment: Good third in the Cornwallis and Breeders' Cup race; 1-1 over 6f; could go well
runners.spotlight: Proved well ahead of his mark in sole handicap attempt and only start over 6f, then finished a good third in the Cornwallis (behind Beckford's Folly) and the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint; receives weight all round and could go well.

quotes.race: Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint (Grade 1) (2yo) (Turf)
quotes.quote: It was a fantastic run. Aspect Island is improving all the time and he's come a long way since Yarmouth. Tasleet improved; he got quicker. He's a big horse, but he handled this well. We've learned a bit and he's learned a good bit as well, so we'll be looking forward to next year with him - James Owen, trainer.

racecards.verdict: Kept to Newmarket, BECKFORD'S FOLLY could well become the first 3yo to win this race for three decades. Quinault is second pick.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Time For Sandals, 11/2 Aramram, 13/2 Beckford's Folly, 8/1 Jasour,  Washington Heights, 9/1 Quinault, 12/1 Completely Random,  Prince Of India, 14/1 Diligent Harry,  Elmonjed, 20/1 Crestofdistinction, 25/1 My Mate Alfie,  Run To Freedom,  Aspect Island

runners.comment: Two from two, both starts at Doncaster; collared Hankelow in Listed grade latest
runners.spotlight: Two from two last year, both starts over 7f at Doncaster, latest in Listed grade (on good ground) when collaring Hankelow on the line despite still seeming green; may have plenty of further progress in him, especially over this extra furlong; one of the main players.

quotes.race: Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Avicenna is learning on the job, was strong through the line and is a horse to look forward to. He's always looked a good horse and we felt he took a good step forward at home since that first run. He'll get a mile, whether this year or next. I think he'll probably be a miler, I don't know whether he's good enough for a Guineas, he's just won a Listed by a nose. He's a nice horse, we don't need to get carried away yet - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He needs more match practice and is likely to run in either the Craven or the Greenham. I've been really happy with him in the last fortnight and we're hopeful that he could be a Guineas candidate of some description. He's in the English, Irish, French and German 2,000 Guineas, and how he runs in Craven week will dictate the next step. I think he'll get a mile well and he's done nothing wrong so far. There's no reason why we can't get excited. 01-04-26

He's a nice horse, he's done nothing wrong and is two from two having won the Flying Scotsman at Doncaster recently. I didn't think he'd won watching it live. I was probably 50 yards short of the finish line and I didn't think he could make up the ground, but he got the head bob. He was very willing under William Buick and we can take a lot away from that. I'm delighted that having received yearlings from the Godolphin team and Sheikh Mohammed for the first time, the first horse that we've got on the track is a tidy performer. That's very satisfying. I'd like to run him again this season but I'm not sure in which race yet. I don't think he's an autumn-ground horse - William thought he just got away with it at Doncaster. He isn't in the Dewhurst or the Lagardere and they're probably unlikely, unless he's supplemented, but he has come out of his last race really well and I don't want to put a line through running him again. I've got to speak to the team, but I might entertain the idea of something like the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf. He's definitely going to stay a mile but I don't think he's ready for an autumn mile. The Autumn Stakes is often won by a middle-distance horse, for example. I think he could stay at 7f or a two-turn American mile on fast ground could suit him, so we'll have that in the back of our minds and see how he progresses over the next fortnight or so. 24-09-25

runners.breeder: S A S Haute Vallee, Mme Moa Sundstrom
runners.comment: His ceiling is seemingly already known and he doesn't have a Guineas entry
runners.spotlight: Record of 2-7 and broadly consistent last term; creditable second in last three starts, including in 7f Group 3 at Newmarket; however, his ceiling is seemingly already known and, unlike all of today's rivals, he doesn't have a 2,000 Guineas entry.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Commander's Intent showed a good attitude there and he always felt like he was just doing enough, especially when we got close late on. He galloped out very strong. It's a good performance off that rating and off this weight and he could yet be of stakes quality - Callum Shepherd, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Commander's Intent is a lovely horse, a colt who definitely stood out in the spring. He was obviously very green on debut but learnt from that experience and the step up in trip and the slight ease in the ground helped - David Egan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Made all in Group 3 over C&D on last appearance; progressive and has solid claims
runners.spotlight: Night Of Thunder colt who nearly went 3-3 last season, the sole defeat when nabbed by Avicenna on the line at Doncaster; justified favouritism in the Autumn Stakes over C&D (good to firm; Group 3) next time, making all; progressive and holds solid claims.

quotes.race: Emirates Autumn Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Hankelow has got such a great mind on him and can only get better. I think he will be better on a more level track - I'll see what Cliff (Lee, jockey) says - and certainly with more juice in the ground. He didn't have the best preps going into Doncaster last time. It was nothing major, but it was just a bit stop-start for the two or three weeks before. I think that is what got him beat that day. The step up in trip suited him today. You only have to look at him going round the prelims to see he is a very relaxed horse. He a good horse. Whether he is quick enough for a Guineas or whether we step up to a mile and a quarter - we have plenty of time to think about that - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: He's never even had a gallop away from home, but is a beautiful horse - as he's entitled to be as Hankelow cost a lot of money. He's shown plenty of ability at home without overdoing himself and he'll improve a bundle. I wouldn't run him on anything quicker than it was at this stage. He'll stay and over a mile I'd say he's a Group horse in the making - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A proper high-class colt who's really starting to work and look well. He's on target for the Guineas, providing the ground is right as he doesn't want it firm. He was going to go straight there but he's further forward than I thought, so he might go to the Craven. If it's obvious he's not going to be quick enough for a Guineas, we've still got plenty of time to go for the Dante or something like that. 31-03-26

runners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
runners.comment: Made all in the Futurity to complete a 1m hat-trick; improving colt who is the form pick
runners.spotlight: Made all and did enough to beat two stablemates in the Futurity at Doncaster (heavy; Group 1) to complete a 1m hat-trick and take record to 3-4; may ideally need further this year, especially when the ground isn't testing; otherwise the form pick and an improving Ballydoyle colt to boot.

quotes.race: William Hill Futurity Trophy Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: I'd say Mountain Hawk is a Classic horse that could start off being a miler and go on up to a mile and a quarter/a mile and a half. He's a classy horse, he gets a mile well and he's tough. He's a massive horse, a big, powerful strong horse. He has an unbelievable mind and he's very straightforward to do everything with. You couldn't be happier with him, he's one of those nice, uncomplicated, powerful big horses. He's big but he's athletic. - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Hawk Mountain travelled like a nice horse through the race. For a few strides when Wayne [Lordan] came beside me I hit a bit of a flat spot but that's all it was. Once I got going again I always felt like I was winning. It was just a matter of keeping him together. He felt like he was still a bit green and I felt there was plenty left in him - Ronan Whelan, jockey.

quotes.race: Qatar Racing & Equestrian Club Beresford Stakes (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.quote: As soon as I got a backhander into Hawk Mountain, he just came alive underneath me. He was very strong at the line. He even spotted something at the line and pricked his ears, so he had loads left. He'll be a middle-distance horse next year, but I definitely think he has the class to go a mile and a quarter. That will open up options for him and he'll have no problem going a mile and a half. He's versatile ground-wise and got through that ground very well today - Ronan Whelan, jockey.Hawk Mountain is a smashing colt. Obviously, he's got the sire and the dam [Wootton Bassett out of Hydrangea], and he has plenty of size and scope. Whatever he does at two we think will be a bonus. He's in the mix for the Futurity Trophy in Doncaster or maybe he could go to France, the race at Saint-Cloud. He's one to look forward to for middle distances next year - Chris Armstrong, trainer's representative.

quotes.race: John Ormonde Wexford Sand Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Big, rangy, relaxed horse, could be anything in time. Wayne (Lordan) says Hawk Mountain was very green but has the makings of a lovely horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He won three last year, including the Futurity Trophy at Doncaster. He went very well at the Curragh on Sunday. Dean [Gallagher] rode him and he was very happy with him. Ryan worked him during the week too and was very happy. He'll be trained for Epsom or France, but listening to the lads he could go for the French Derby and have a trial for it. He'd be very comfortable at a mile and a quarter and is a very good horse. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Two from two, namely AW wins at Kempton, latest in a notable conditions race; respected
runners.spotlight: Frankel colt who is two from two, namely AW wins at Kempton, last time comfortably beating Venetian Prince in 1m conditions race that his yard landed in 2024 and 2025 with subsequent Group 1 scorers (including 2,000 Guineas); the signs look very good for this highly promising sort.

runners.comment: Chance of opening his Group account depends on the effects of first-time headgear
runners.spotlight: Unsuited by heavy ground in the Futurity on final 2yo start; steadily progressive otherwise, and ran well in the Champagne Stakes at Doncaster and Dewhurst at Newmarket; however, chance of opening his Group account largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear.

runners.comment: Unlikely to reverse Kempton placings with Hidden Force but again could go well
runners.spotlight: Scored at Newbury when last seen on turf; looked flattered to finished just under 2l behind Hidden Force, who had something in hand, at Kempton most recently and is unlikely to reverse the placings; however, bred to do better still and may produce another good effort.

racecards.verdict: Hawk Mountain is respected on the figures but he may be done for finishing kick by the promising HIDDEN FORCE in this scenario.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Hawk Mountain, 5/2 Hidden Force, 9/2 Avicenna,  Hankelow, 10/1 Oxagon, 20/1 Venetian Prince, 25/1 Commander's Intent

runners.comment: Runner-up all three starts (7f, AW) and she sets the standard; turf debut
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in three starts, all over this trip at Chelmsford (AW); doesn't look to be doing anything wrong in a finish and sets the standard on form; contender again with nothing in her pedigree suggesting this switch to turf will be a problem.

runners.comment: 52,000gns yearling by Sea The Stars; market might help ahead of this debut
runners.spotlight: 52,000gns yearling by Sea The Stars; twelfth foal; half-sister to seven winners including Pimento (Group-placed 1m AW including 2yo; RPR 112), White Bullet (6f AW; 87), Zakreet (7f/1m 2yo; 86) and Valkyrja (1m; 71); dam unraced sister to 11.4f Listed winner Birdie; market might help ahead of this debut.

runners.comment: Night Of Thunder filly; 3rd in 6f Windsor fillies' novice (good) in June; player on return
runners.spotlight: Night Of Thunder filly; dam 6f and 7f (Group 2) 2yo winner/1,000 Guineas second (116); 13-2 when encouraging third of nine in 6f Windsor fillies' novice (good) in June; not seen since but almost certainly has best days ahead of her and any market confidence could prove telling.

runners.owner: L J Vaessen And Stephen Barber
runners.comment: By Zoustar; dam 7f/1m winner (93); unlikely newcomer but market check advised
runners.spotlight: By Zoustar; half-sister to 6f AW winner Lord Danielson (RPR 57); dam 7f/1m winner (including AW; 93), sister to UAE 1m winner Pictograph, out of unraced half-sister to 1m2f-1m4f Group 1 winner Vengeance Of Rain; stable not a noted source of winning newcomers but worth a market check.

runners.comment: Blue Point filly from family of star colt Almanzor; key debutante for leading connections
runners.spotlight: Blue Point fifth foal; half-sister to winners Yaanaas (1m AW; RPR 99) and Orionis (1m3f-1m4f; 97); dam French Listed-placed 9.5f/1m4f winner (99), sister to 1m2f/10.5f Group 1 winner Almanzor; market will reveal more but she's a likely contender for leading connections.

runners.comment: 240,000gns foal by Pinatubo; raw when fifth on sole start last year; better on the cards
runners.spotlight: 240,000gns foal by Pinatubo; looked raw but plugged on late when fifth of nine in Salisbury maiden (7f, good) in October; yard among the winners and she's surely capable of better.

racecards.verdict: A chance is taken that THURSDAY GIRL has learned plenty from her debut at Salisbury last year.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Hassaleh, 2/1 Pointe Bleu, 5/1 Baandee, 6/1 Thursday Girl, 8/1 Eloquencia, 50/1 La Mariposa

racecards.race_name: Betway EBF "Confined" Novice Stakes (For horses Which Have Run No More Than Once) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
runners.comment: 10-11, won Curragh maiden (7f, good) last June in a five-way scrap; Dante and Derby entry
runners.spotlight: By Wootton Bassett out of a Galileo mare; 10-11 for maiden at the Curragh (7f, good) last June and always prominent to win that ten-runner race by half a length in a five-way scrap, but he has not raced since; stablemate in second was useful afterwards but the third showed no better than fair form; a promising Dante and Derby entry, for whom the market may guide.

stable_tour.quote: He won his only race last year in a 7f maiden at the Curragh in June. He's out of a Galileo mare and is the type for a Derby trial. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Green when winning narrowly from out the back in a maiden at Haydock (7f, good) last July
runners.spotlight: 240,000euros yearling; by Sea The Moon out of a close relation to 1m2f Group 1 winner Sultanina; second favourite for seven-runner maiden at Haydock (7f, good) last July, which he nearly blew when making an awkward start and first off the bridle but he came from the back and stuck his neck out well for a narrow win; absent since but should be open to major improvement.

quotes.race: MB Health EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Birgham Dub is a talented racehorse. He was green from the stalls and I was quite a long way back off a slow pace. I just popped him out with about three and a half [furlongs] to give him a good sighter of where he needed to go and he picked up very well. Jane [Chapple-Hyam, trainer] said he's got a beautiful temperament and he's very straightforward and he proved that. There should be some improvement to come - Hector Crouch, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Fav, 3l win at Lingfield (1m, AW) in December despite looking green; Dante and Derby entry
runners.spotlight: 325,000gns yearling by Teofilo; ninth foal; brother to four winners including Group winners Guaranteed (RPR 109) and Gear Up (114); 13-8 favourite for novice at Lingfield (1m, AW) in December and came from fifth of 12 at halfway to win by  3l, despite looking green; Dante and Derby entry from a top yard, who'll surely stay and find plenty of improvement this term.

quotes.race: Win £250,000 With BetMGM's Golden Goals Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: He's a nice horse. He's a work in progress. The lads said that Guildmaster spent the whole time on his back legs in the pre-parade ring. He was green in the race as well, on and off the bridle, and will definitely get ten furlongs. He might be the type to run in another novice with a penalty - Robert Havlin, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Kempton win (1m3f, AW; 5-6) in December came with great authority; Dante and Derby entry
runners.spotlight: By Dubawi; third foal; half-brother to winners Cavallo Bay (Group-placed 7f 2yo; RPR 101) and Spring Beauty (French 5.5f); dam 6f/1m 2yo winner (including Canadian turf Grade 1; 106); 5-6 for five-runner maiden at Kempton (1m3f, AW) in December, leading 2f out for a 6l win; that came with great authority, so this Dante and Derby entry looks a good prospect.

runners.breeder: Newsells Park Stud & Merry Fox Stud
runners.comment: 180,000gns yearling by Galiway; Dante entry, so needs a close look despite debut
runners.spotlight: 180,000gns yearling by Galiway; fifth foal; closely related to 1m1f-1m2f winner Integrant (including AW Listed; RPR 108), half-brother to French 9.5f winner Viatore; dam Group-placed 7f/1m 2yo winner (103), half-sister to Group 3 winners at 7f and 1m; trainer won this last year with another Dante (and Derby) entry and this debutant needs a close look.

runners.comment: 46l defeat at Southwell (1m3f, AW; 14-1) five days ago suggests he faces a very stiff task
runners.spotlight: Camelot half-brother to five winners, notably Bolshoi Ballet (1m-1m4f including US Grade 1; RPR 119); 46l defeat at Southwell (1m3f, AW; 14-1) five days ago suggests he faces a very stiff task.

racecards.verdict: Charlie Appleby has won five of the eight runnings of this race and his MAHO BAY looks a good starting point for calculations this time.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Maho Bay, 15/8 Amadeus Mozart, 7/2 Guildmaster, 8/1 Birgham Dub, 10/1 Galiyan, 100/1 Sir Griflet

racecards.race_name: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap

runners.breeder: C R Marks & R J Gallagher
runners.comment: Needs to be near best to make a winning comeback but beaten a nose on last year's return
runners.spotlight: Progressed last term; pick of her efforts came when fourth in AW Group 3 (6f) in June and when beating all bar Royal Velvet in July course handicap (7f, good to firm) the following month; will need to be near her best to make a winning seasonal debut but was beaten only a nose on last year's return.

runners.comment: Absent 20 months but h'capper has given him a shot and yard going well; watch the market
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in this race in 2024 when it was staged as a Class 2; made all at Chester (7.5f, good to firm) on his next start and it was a solid fourth back there (7f, good to soft) when last seen 20 months ago; yard going well and handicapper has given him a shot too; watch the market.

quotes.race: CAA Stellar Earl Grosvenor Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a great ride by Richard, and Percy's Lad proved in the race last year he can get out of a high draw well [finished third]. We'll see how he comes out of this and there's a race back here in a couple of weeks and he could go back for the Buckingham Palace - Claire Kubler, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Handicap
quotes.quote: I popped into the Kublers' last week and I've known Daniel for a long time. The plan was to follow something else on Percy's Lad but I was a passenger so I decided to come over to the stands' rail. He did that well and was entitled to win like that on his two-year-old form - Richard Kingscote, jockey.

quotes.race: Call Star Sports On 08000521321 Derby "Wild Card" Conditions Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Percy's Lad has a lot of pace so I'm not convinced he'll stay the Derby trip, but we'll see. He'd be seen at his best in a bigger field with a better pace to aim at but I'm absolutely thrilled with him. It probably wasn't a particularly strong renewal but he could only win it and he's a nice horse. - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He ran a blinder at Newmarket the other day, which should set him up nicely for Chester's May meeting next week. He was beaten by what looks a very smart horse [Poet Master] and was more tractable, so maybe he's grown up, which would make life easier for his jockeys. He runs well at Chester and holds a course record, while he was third in the race we're aiming for from a bad draw last year. There's a good programme for him at Chester, so he could spend quite a bit of time there as the track suits. He wasn't beaten far in the Buckingham Palace at Royal Ascot last year, but we may shoot lower, albeit still at a tidy level. 02-05-24

runners.comment: Just 1lb above last win and fit from AW; could make his presence felt
runners.spotlight: Soft-ground Sandown winner in August who is just 1lb higher; comes here fit after two respectable fourth-place finishes at Kempton (also 7f, AW); acts on this forecast good ground and could make his presence felt.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a cracker at Chester last week, just getting touched off by El Burhan, and seemed to handle the track well. He's been doing a lot of his training with Harvard Sound as they're similar types. He's in good form. 14-05-25

runners.comment: Hard to ignore his last win came back in June 2023 (7f G3) but returns on reduced mark
runners.spotlight: C&D winner who could only beat one home in this race when it was staged as a Class 2 last year; managed a handful of creditable efforts subsequently but it's hard to ignore his last win came back in June 2023 (7f Group 3); returns on reduced mark.

quotes.race: Sky Bet John Of Gaunt Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Seven furlongs is the right trip, but it's the hardest trip to find and Jumby also doesn't want soft ground, so we have to just pick our way through. He's a brilliant horse who is very good in Group 3s, he's won a Group 2 and there's no reason why he couldn't win another one. He'd have to carry a lot of weight in the Wokingham, but when you see the size of him I don't think weight bothers him very much, so we'll see - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

quotes.race: BetVictor Hungerford Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Jumby has won it like a proper horse. I've always thought he had the pace for six furlongs, but not the gate speed. He's growing up and is a big horse. His form's there to be seen and he could even go a mile, but he loves fast ground and running at horses after a good pace. I'll enter in the Prix de la Foret, but we need to see what the ground is like and he's in the City of York next week, and I'm not ruling it out yet. We could then think about Dubai and Bahrain - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

quotes.race: Wokingham Stakes (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I'm thrilled. I thought we'd won it. We might run Jumby back quick in the Criterion over seven - I think he wants seven because you can hang on to him longer and you don't need to use that turn of foot. We might go for the Bunbury Cup otherwise and he wants this ground - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

quotes.race: Heed Your Hunch At Betway Handicap
quotes.quote: Jumby's form looked strong after Creative Force won at Newbury earlier and he got the job done. We were a bit worried about the ground but it was perfect in the end - William Buick, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He just got in the Wokingham - he was the last one in and I was very happy with that. He loves 7f but doesn't get it at Ascot - it's a bit stiff for him there but he was third in the Wokingham three years ago and ran a lovely race this time too, finishing tenth. He never lets us down but is still a bit high in the handicap for an old boy. As to where we'll go later on, he used to love the Hungerford. He won it in 2022 and was third last year, only beaten a nose and a short head, but we'll have to see whether he's good enough to go back there this year. He's entered in the Bunbury Cup and it's a possible. He loves 7f really but a stiff 6f suits him as well. 02-07-25

runners.comment: 3-4 since asked to tackle 7f; big fields no problem; can likely do better again this term
runners.spotlight: 3-4 since asked to tackle 7f from late August with wins at Newbury (good) and twice on AW (latterly dead-heating); big fields no problem and he can likely do better again this term; player if tuned up.

runners.comment: Steady improver who scored three times last year; should be ready and she's much respected
runners.spotlight: Steady improver who scored three times last year, including here (1m) in May and on the July course (7f, also good to firm) two months later; also landed valuable big-field fillies' handicap at York which bodes well for this test; should be ready to roll on this return and she's much respected.

quotes.race: Trustatrader 20th Anniversary Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: I'm delighted for Royal Velvet's owner-breeder Susie Hartley. Going back to 7f from a mile has been the right decision and having William on board always helps, particularly at this track - William Knight, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet £10 Get £40 With BetMGM Handicap
quotes.quote: They went a bit quick up front because of the loose horse. Royal Velvet basically picked up the pieces - Cieren Fallon, jockey.

quotes.race: Bet £5 Get £20 At tote.co.uk Racing League Race 3 Handicap (Trainers Registered To Racing League)
quotes.quote: Royal Velvet has won really well there today. I did think the flat track and the easy mile really suits her and she likes that ground. She was quite backward last year and she's just really coming to herself. I think she could be quite useful - William Knight, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Won in big field; plenty of potential ahead of this comeback on just fourth handicap start
runners.spotlight: Good-ground maiden winner on his April return last year and it was a good run after a break when third of 14 at Newcastle (also 6f, AW) in August; signed off by beating 14 others at Leicester (7f, good) in October after which he was gelded; retains plenty of potential ahead of this comeback on just his fourth handicap start.

quotes.race: Flat Is Back Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We wait all winter looking for the green stuff, so it's lovely to come to Nottingham and win the first race. Storm Free was a maiden in all but name really because he'd been a close second the last twice - James Tate, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's been steadily progressive and we like him. He should have won his maiden last year but he used to break a little bit slow and had a couple of seconds instead. He broke a bit better first time out this year and won nicely at Nottingham in April. He's had a little niggly setback that has kept him off but we think he's better than his rating of 83 and so he should be one to follow when he's next out, which will probably be towards the end of this month. 09-07-25

runners.owner: B Jordan, Brian Jordan, S Jordan & N McConnell

prev_owners.owner: Brian Jordan, B Jordan & Stephen Jordan
Brian Jordan, B Jordan & Stephen Jordan

runners.comment: Admirable old boy but no win last year and return was poor; tries 7f for the first time
runners.spotlight: Admirable old boy who had a sparkling 2024, winning seven times (5f/6f, sound surface) mostly at Hamilton; couldn't add to that haul last year, though, and never figured when last on his recent reappearance (soft ground admittedly against him); tries 7f for the first time on this 84th start.

quotes.race: Aspire At Hamilton-Park Handicap
quotes.quote: The problem is with William [Buick] he's that good he wins by too far! He's rode me a winner or two over the years and he's obviously a first-class jockey. It was amazing for Jordan Electrics to do what he did carrying so much weight. He's superb to train; at one time he was difficult to travel, but he's mellowing as he gets older. We'll probably come back here for the Scottish Stewards' Cup next - Jim Goldie, trainer.
