stable_tour.quote: Unfortunately he picked up an injury so he's going to be off for the first half of the season, but we're thinking he'll be back and it's not career-ending. He's sound but he's going to need time to get over what happened. We'd like to win an Ayr Gold Cup, so we'll target that and possibly the Portland. That's a fickle double, it's usually one or the other. He's a grand horse. Technically at his age he's supposed to be diminishing but he doesn't seem to be. The man who feeds him rides him and he's managed very well. He's a Hamilton specialist. It's probably going to be a bit more difficult for him now, but he's thereabouts in those top sprints. 07-05-25

runners.comment: Improved in headgear over 7f last term (three wins); not ruled out on this reappearance
runners.spotlight: Improved in headgear over 7f last term, winning in first-time cheekpieces on the July course (good to firm) in June and in a newly fitted visor at Southwell in August; also scored in latter aid at Chelmsford (also AW) in October; slight worry slow starts were a feature of his last two runs but might have needed a rest by then; not ruled out on this reappearance.

runners.comment: Won twice for Dermot Weld; left that yard for 150,000gns; first try at 7f and unexposed
runners.spotlight: Won at the Curragh (1m1f) on seasonal/handicap debut in June and doubled his tally in Killarney conditions event (1m, also good) in August; big disappointment on final start for Dermot Weld in late September but new connections had to go to 150,000gns to secure him one month later; unexposed and interesting to see how he goes in the market ahead of this first start at 7f.

quotes.race: Dubai Duty Free Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Chris [Hayes] had Sujet in a lovely position throughout. When you are drawn wide here it is important to go and get a position otherwise you will be forced very wide over the nine furlongs, but he got him out and got him over. He tracked Ryan (Moore, on leader Mississippi Rover) and the plan was to have a go at him in the final furlong and that is just what he did. We'll see how he comes out of the race and another handicap will be the plan for him. He was gelded and just took a bit of time to come to himself. This was a lovely race for a three-year-old and he had been working nicely - Dermot Weld, trainer.

runners.comment: Prolific on AW for new yard and two wins in Ireland came in big fields on a sound surface
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish gelding who has been productive on AW in cheekpieces this winter for James Owen; went back-to-back at Newcastle (6f) in December and secured a four-timer when scoring at Lingfield (1m; first three legs at 7f) last month; creditable third back on turf (7f, good to soft) last time and his two wins on turf in Ireland came in big fields on a sound surface; considered.

quotes.race: Tote.ie Handicap
quotes.quote: Goldmoyne loves this place but getting him to the start is the problem as he gets very wound up. If you can get him to the start in the right frame of mind he has ability - Tim Doyle, trainer

quotes.race: Sycamore Lodge Equine Hospital Handicap
quotes.quote: Goldmoyne is a horse with a lot of ability but he is also very headstrong. I thought he had a chance if he did things right. He is very tough though and he found when they came to him - Tim Doyle, trainer.

runners.comment: Started last term well; above last winning mark but can feature if returning in same vein
runners.spotlight: Started last term very well; third of 21 at York (good) in May followed by hat-trick of wins (also 7f, good to firm) across June and July; remains 4lb above his last winning mark but could feature if returning in similar vein.

quotes.race: Star Sports We Believe In Bookmaking Handicap
quotes.quote: You haven't seen Crimson Spirit at his best there. He went to go and win his race and then got blown around a bit, got unbalanced and the second horse just lunged at him a bit. I thought he did well in difficult circumstances and it was more a case of job done than seeing what he could do - Richard Kingscote, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Crimson Spirit was always in a nice rhythm. He wasn't trying to run to freely early on. He got a nice flow through, found a little gap and picked up nicely. The ground was much nicer than at Nottingham. I was pleased with the way he took me down that hill. We should have some fun with him next year as well - Richard Kingscote, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He ran really well on his reappearance at York. He's a lovely, big, scopey gelding with lots to look forward to as the season progresses. He handles any track, he's versatile and he's a fun horse who should be winning more races. We're looking at Salisbury for him on Sunday. 11-06-25

runners.comment: Dual 7f winner; big effort over 5f on recent stable debut; has to be of interest
runners.spotlight: Dual 7f (good/good to yielding) winner in Ireland who was soon outpaced before coming home strongly to be beaten a whisker in 5f Scottish Sprint Cup (soft) 12 days ago; that was a really encouraging first go for Jim Goldie and this step back up to 7f should be fine; has to be of interest.

quotes.race: Golf At Gowran Park Handicap
quotes.quote: Gangsta Man was a bit unlucky in a couple of his runs and he probably deserved that. He had a nice draw here and he kind of got the luck in running. There are no plans with him as of yet. The plan was to bring him to the horse in training sales at Newmarket, so I don't know if he will run again between now and then - Kevin Smith, trainer.

runners.comment: Went close three times at 7f last term; returns on a competitive-looking mark
runners.spotlight: Two wins as a juvenile (6f, good/good to firm); couldn't add to that tally last year but he was gelded in May and went close three times at 7f (good to firm/AW) subsequently; returns on a competitive-looking mark and he's considered.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C & D) (Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: It was a good run at Goodwood in a stronger race than this. Huscal was learning on the job that day and the only question mark was that Ripon can be difficult for inexperienced horses. He travels, which helps when you hit a few of those ridges. He's not the finished article and should keep on improving - James Doyle, jockey.

runners.comment: Respectable on both starts last month and Oisin Murphy takes over for the first time
runners.spotlight: Kept fairly busy in the last 12 months and he supplemented a 6f Windsor (good) win in September by scoring over 7f at Yarmouth (good to soft) in October and at Chelmsford (AW) in December; respectable efforts on both starts last month and Oisin Murphy takes over for the first time.

stable_tour.quote: He's always been a laid-back character and I'm really pleased with how he's done over the winter. He had nowhere to go on his comeback at Kempton and hopefully he can move forward from that run and have better luck next time. He wouldn't want it too soft, is versatile at six or seven furlongs and I hope he can keep progressing. 02-05-23

He has only won the once but he has run consistently well in defeat apart from last time at Newmarket where he got a bit behind the pace and that cost him any chance. His penultimate run behind Quinault at York reads well and I'm looking at going back to the July course if conditions are in his favour and it dries out as he is not far off winning again. He may even run in the Stewards' Cup on Saturday. 02-08-23

runners.comment: Weak in the market for his stable debut when it all went wrong at the start 19 days ago
runners.spotlight: First-time blinkers when making all for easy win in Epsom novice (7f, soft) in September 2024; encouraging return from a year's absence the following October but he left Ralph Beckett after a moderate effort next time; weak in the market for his stable debut when it all went wrong at the start 19 days ago.

runners.comment: Good 2yo and latest third was encouraging; suspicion he could be on the way back
runners.spotlight: Yet to match his 2yo best (included big sales race and Listed wins) but he's only had eight subsequent starts and latest third at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) four weeks ago was a firm step back in the right direction; same mark and there's a suspicion he could be on the way back; player if so.

quotes.race: William Hill Two Year Old Trophy (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Clive has campaigned Dragon Leader beautifully, he's a sweet, likeable horse. He was getting a weight off a lot of them, which was a big help, and he's won some nice pots this year - Richard Kingscote, jockey.

quotes.race: Goffs UK Harry Beeby Premier Yearling Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That's three from three for Dragon Leader so it's no surprise but to do it quite as comfortably as he did was great. Ryan is top drawer but a lot of thanks goes to John Fahy who worked very hard on this horse in the spring. We've got a lot to consider. His medium value qualifies him well for a few races, so there's some good prize-money angles to think about. We'll be thinking properly about Group company as well - Clive Cox, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won a couple of valuable races as a two-year-old and has been gelded and had a small wind operation after disappointing last season. He's been training nicely but was drawn badly in stall 14 in the Spring Cup at Newbury on Saturday. Hopefully, he can come forward for the run and improve next time. 17-04-25

He has won over £300,000 and has slightly paid for that success this season, although he ran a mighty race to finish tenth in the Britannia at Royal Ascot and has been dropped 2lb since, so he's feasibly handicapped. But his work has been a bit indifferent and Clive wants to see the old Dragon Leader at home. He might come back to 7f to make use of his good gate speed and he has two options over that trip at Glorious Goodwood. 02-08-24

runners.comment: Big Galway handicap win for this trainer in 2024; might step forward from recent comeback
runners.spotlight: C&D novice winner back in the day and he was trained by Micky Fenton in Ireland when landing big Galway handicap (7f, heavy) in 2024; back with his former trainer (in Newmarket this time) when weakening over 6f at Doncaster 18 days ago; might step forward from that comeback.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Ahonoora Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Physique is a horse who likes to get on with things and there is only one way to ride him. He can get quite wound up if you try to hold him back. Seamie knows him and knew what to do after riding him the last couple of times - Micky Fenton, trainer.

racecards.verdict: Loads to consider not least STORM FREE who is unexposed but has already proven himself in big fields.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Storm Free, 6/1 Huscal,  Gangsta Man, 8/1 Goldmoyne, 9/1 Royal Velvet, 10/1 Dragon Leader,  Morte Point, 12/1 Eminency, 14/1 Crimson Spirit, 16/1 Physique,  Sujet, 20/1 Percy's Lad,  Jumby,  God Of War, 25/1 Dapper Guest, 33/1 Jordan Electrics,  Havana Pusey, 50/1 Bold Impact

racecards.race_name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Promising third on sole 2yo start but disappointing at Pontefract nine days ago
runners.spotlight: Fared best of the newcomers when promising third at Redcar (6f, good) last October; far too soon to write him off but he was disappointing at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) nine days ago, even allowing for a wide trip.

runners.comment: Good 2nd on debut last June; two lesser runs followed but leading claims if back to best
runners.spotlight: Good second on debut at Ayr (6f, good) last June; two lesser runs followed last year but he's from a useful sprinting family and is a leading contender if back to his best in a first-time hood, following a break.

runners.comment: Runner-up on debut on AW three weeks ago; could have plenty more to offer
runners.spotlight: Weak in the betting but still ran well when runner-up at 13-2 on debut at Chelmsford (6f, AW) three weeks ago; his dam was a useful 6f winner and he could have plenty more to offer; firmly in calculations.

runners.comment: Improvement possible but soundly beaten at 16-1 on his recent debut at Pontefract
runners.spotlight: 10,000gns foal whose unraced dam is from a speedy family; improvement is possible on this second start but he was soundly beaten at 16-1 at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) on his recent debut and needs a big step forward.

runners.comment: Has shown promise for top yard and the drop in trip could suit on his third start
runners.spotlight: Runner-up on debut at Chelmsford (7f, AW) last March then failed to build on it when fourth at Southwell (7f, AW); however, he's in top hands and his pedigree suggests the drop in trip will suit; wears first-time blinkers and he remains one to be interested in.

runners.comment: Down the field at big odds this year on his first two starts (6f/7f, AW)
runners.spotlight: Down the field at big odds this year on his first two starts (6f/7f, AW) and considerable improvement is necessary.

runners.comment: Eyecatching third on debut at Newcastle last month and could be sharper for that outing
runners.spotlight: 14-1, recovered from slow start to finish third of 11 on debut at Newcastle (6f, AW) four weeks ago; it's possible a longer trip will be preference but he could be sharper for that initial outing and is respected.

runners.comment: Half-brother to three winners; sole newcomer; interesting to see how he goes in betting
runners.spotlight: Ninth foal; Tasleet half-brother to winners Akeed Dubawi (1m AW; RPR 80), Tarnhelm (6f-1m; 72) and Billy McGarry (7f-8.6f; 66); dam 5f 2yo winner (90); sole newcomer but interesting to see how he goes in the betting.

racecards.verdict: The attractively bred THE UNTAMED was a promising second on last month's debut at Chelmsford and is taken to go one better.
racecards.betting_forecast: 10/11 The Untamed, 4/1 Vega Storm, 5/1 Mind Over Matter,  Different Opinions, 16/1 Milford Grange, 33/1 Agric Ranger,  Tickhill Flyer, 100/1 Kode Grey

racecards.race_name: Download The Raceday Ready App Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 4yo who was fourth on AW on recent belated debut; could take step forward; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: 4yo who made belated debut at Southwell (1m4f, AW) 11 days ago and was beaten 7l in fourth of nine; improvement is necessary but he's a half-brother to the yard's useful 1m2f-1m4f winner Real Terms and may well be able to take a step forward; not ruled out.

runners.comment: 33,000gns yearling by Sea The Moon; could give a good account on debut
runners.spotlight: 33,000gns yearling; third foal; dam 1m/8.6f AW winner (RPR 99), half-sister to useful winners Spangler (7f/1m including 2yo) and Kipps (1m2f 2yo); this Sea The Moon colt could give a good account on debut.

runners.comment: Useful pedigree and this Almanzor newcomer is one to consider
runners.spotlight: Fourth foal; Almanzor brother to French 1m2f 2yo winner The Sheriff, closely related to 1m2f-1m4f winner Wootton'sun (RPR 101); dam French 1m4f Flat/2m1f hurdle winner from classy family; this newcomer is one to consider.

runners.comment: Third over 1m here on sole 2yo start; pedigree suggests that he will relish this trip
runners.spotlight: Having been outpaced he kept on for a promising third at 8-1 on debut here (1m, good to firm) last August; gelded since; his pedigree suggests that he will relish this step up in trip on his reappearance; strong contender.

runners.comment: There's potential in his pedigree but well beaten at big odds last month on first two runs
runners.spotlight: There's potential in his pedigree but he was well beaten at big odds last month on his first two starts (1m4f/9.4f, AW).

runners.comment: First foal; dam French 11.7f winner; could have a part to play on debut; watch the betting
runners.spotlight: £10,000 yearling by Havana Gold; first foal; dam French 11.7f winner, half-sister to French 6.5f/7f winner Zalari, out of 1m Listed winner; Newmarket trainer is 2-10 with his Ripon runners; could have a part to play on debut, especially if strong in the betting.

runners.comment: Tackles different trip on second start but always behind at 40-1 on debut in February (1m)
runners.spotlight: Pedigree indicates that the step up in trip will be in his favour but he was reluctant to load and always behind when 40-1 on debut at Newcastle (1m, AW) in February; may be best watched for now.

racecards.verdict: The Karl Burke-trained URCHIN was a promising third over 1m here on his sole 2yo start and is bred to come into his own over this trip.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/8 Urchin, 4/1 Picaro, 9/2 Poppeye,  Sun Lord, 11/2 Sea And Sun, 100/1 N'Ion,  Rocky River

runners.comment: Two wins last summer before coming up short in good company; mark looks tough enough
runners.spotlight: Two wins last summer, a 5.5f maiden at Wetherby (good to firm) and a 5f nursery at Haydock (good), before coming up short in two sales races and the Listed Two-Year-Old Trophy; still has time on her side but not obviously well handicapped back from 194 days off.

runners.comment: Had some useful 2yo form, including C&D; returns with her yard going well; new headgear
runners.spotlight: Won a Haydock novice on her second start and bumped into a useful opponent over C&D last August; ran well on her handicap debut at Doncaster in September but she ended her 2yo campaign with two lesser efforts; could resume here progress this year and she returns with her stable in good form; cheekpieces make their debut (wore blinkers final 2yo run).

runners.comment: 2-3 as a 2yo, looking a nice prospect; her trainer has won this race four times since 2016
runners.spotlight: Well backed prior to her winning debut at Newcastle (6f) last September; failed to fire in the Redcar Two-Year-Old Trophy on second start but back on the up when defying a penalty in a Leicester novice in October (6f, good); the form of her two victories hasn't really worked out but she could do no more than win in decisive fashion and it is likely she has more to come; interesting for the stable that took this in 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2024.

quotes.race: British EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Storm Esme has had a couple of runs whereas a few of the others were having their first starts. She didn't fly the gates but she was straight on to the bridle and travelled nicely in my hands. I was waiting until she got a bit of company to quicken up, but she went away nicely. She's still a bit raw and learning the game. She showed us plenty even before she ran the first time and she was well backed that day; all the yard fancied her. She was thrown in the deep end in the Two Year Old Trophy at Redcar but she learned a lot from it and was a lot more straightforward today - David Allan, jockey.

runners.comment: Made all in Ayr maiden last July (5.5f, good); fair nursery form afterwards; been gelded
runners.spotlight: Easy front-running win at Ayr (5.5f, good) last July on his third start; showed promise in nurseries afterwards; gelded during his six-month absence; personal best needed but it is not out of the question.

runners.comment: 6f AW win on final run for R Beckett; sold 26,000gns afterwards; opening mark demands more
runners.spotlight: Ran to a similar RPR in three runs for Ralph Beckett as a 2yo, getting off the mark in a small-field 6f novice at Wolverhampton when last seen in October; sold for 26,000gns soon afterwards; capable of better but such progress will be required to defy this mark.

runners.comment: AW maiden win on return but couldn't build on it at Southwell last month; headgear on now
runners.spotlight: Promise as a 2yo and he only had to match that form to make a winning seasonal return at Wolverhampton last month; well backed back in handicap company at Southwell three weeks ago but he was ultimately a shade disappointing; connections now reach for headgear.

prev_owners.owner: Valmont, C Rosier & Mrs J Rosier

runners.comment: 6f AW winner; outstayed over 7f on handicap debut; still has potential for new yard
runners.spotlight: Green on 2yo debut but took a big step forward when winning a 6f novice at Kempton on his second start (well backed); stiff task next time and his subsequent Southwell third (7f) was a solid start to his handicap career; sold out of Oliver Cole's stable for 35,000gns in February and gelded; new connections quick to drop him back to sprint trips and he remains with some potential

runners.comment: Two 6f wins in maiden/novice company; excuses for three nursery defeats; not discounted
runners.spotlight: Won 6f maiden/novice events last August (good/good to firm); unplaced in three nurseries afterwards but two of them were on soft ground and the other was a sound effort at York where 5f looked an inadequate test; gelded since last seen; returns on a reduced mark and one of two to consider for a stable with a fine record in the race.

runners.comment: Won a 6f AW novice for Ed Bethell in December; sold 11,000gns since; mark looks tough
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the fourth attempt when landing a modest fillies' novice (6f) at Newcastle four months ago; sold out of Ed Bethell's for 11,000gns in February; opening mark looks stiff.

runners.breeder: Mrs J A Rawding & Miss A J Rawding
runners.comment: Promise over 5f last autumn; 6f should suit but improvement essential to defy opening mark
runners.spotlight: Two promising runs over 5f for this yard last autumn; stepping up to 6f should be in his favour and he is open to improvement but such progress looks essential if he is to defy this mark.

runners.comment: Promising 7f AW run for former yard; sold 10,000gns in February; likely best watched
runners.spotlight: Placed in a 7f AW novice on his third run as a 2yo; well beaten over a mile when last seen in September; sold out of John Ryan's stable for 10,000gns in February; likely best watched on his stable/handicap debut.

runners.comment: Ran okay in his first three nurseries but he needs to have improved over the winter
runners.spotlight: Won a 5f claimer at Beverley on his second start (last May) and he hit the frame in his first three nursery runs; failed to fire on the slowest ground he had tackled when last seen; needs to have improved over the winter if he is to make a winning return.

quotes.race: Cottingham Claiming Stakes (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Head For Freedom was probably the best bred horse in the race and the bit of cut in the ground helped him. He has been a handful and if it wasn't for Craig Witherford we would never have got him to the race. He came to the yard twice and his techniques were second to none - David Easterby, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: C&D winner; good second on her reappearance last week; well drawn to attack
runners.spotlight: Always prominent when winning a C&D maiden last August; ran her best race in handicaps when second of ten in a 5f event at Catterick (good) last week, keeping on; she will have the stands' rail to help this time and should go well despite stepping up in class.

quotes.race: Squadron Flyer At Aldwark Manor Estate EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C/D) (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Empress Olivia had shown enough at home and she sharpened up for each of her first two runs. We thought she would win and I'd love to say we thought it would be today but we didn't have our money on! We thought it would probably be in a nursery. She's the only 2yo we've run, she travelled really nicely and she was going away at the end - Mark Walford, trainer.

racecards.verdict: Tim Easterby's fine record in this 3yo handicap heightens interest in both STORM ESME and Bye Law.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/1 Generous Rascal,  Storm Esme, 6/1 Empress Olivia, 13/2 Rogue Temptation, 7/1 Hvar, 8/1 Wyle Cop, 10/1 Cotai Belle,  Mighty Magnus, 14/1 Head For Freedom, 16/1 Yy Spirit, 20/1 Bye Law,  Fordham Flyer, 25/1 Wise Crack

runners.comment: Unexposed 4yo; not well drawn on stable/seasonal debut; remains of serious interest
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a good second at Newmarket (6f, good), after which he changed hands for 50,000gns; only eighth (of 19) on his stable debut at Doncaster 18 days ago but he wasn't well drawn as things panned out and he ran as though the run would bring him on; remains a sprinter of interest.

stable_tour.quote: He's a half-brother to Rogue Lightning. He won a novice under a penalty at Doncaster last month and that form looks strong. He might go to Newmarket next for a valuable handicap a week on Saturday. He's got a wonderful attitude and was very resolute at Doncaster - he really put his head down and battled, which is a trait you love to see. He was very laid-back last year and green and backward at Windsor when he made his debut, but the penny has really dropped now. He's done a bit of work with Invictus Gold and I hope he can be a nice flagbearer for the yard throughout the year. 14-05-25

runners.comment: C&D win on this card last year; ended 2025 tamely; likely to be seen to better effect here
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer; C&D winner on his seasonal return on this card 12 months ago; often ran well in good handicaps afterwards and although he ended 2025 with a couple of lesser efforts, he is likely to be seen to much better effect this time; should make a bold bid up the stands' rail.

runners.comment: Low-key return to action last month and may be better suited by 7f+ nowadays
runners.spotlight: C&D winner in 2023 off an 8lb higher mark; all his subsequent wins have come over 7f+ and his return to action at Doncaster was unconvincing; others appeal more.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Training Series Final Apprentice Handicap (Part Of The Racing Excellence Series) (Div II)
quotes.quote: It Just Takes Time made it look easy and relished the ground. It slowed the others down but he's a very simple ride. I popped him out and drop the hands and that's his style. He hits a flat spot but never gives up. He's very game - Olivia Tubb, jockey.

quotes.race: Joe Rowntree Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: It Just Takes Time is still progressing now we have found out how we can keep him settled down. He did that well enough. That was the perfect distance and a sharp 7f suits him well - Jack Garritty, jockey.

runners.comment: On last winning mark and he has run two solid races on AW this year; each-way shout
runners.spotlight: Won a Racing League handicap off this mark last summer; two solid AW efforts this year, keeping on strongly for third in a well-contested 6f handicap at Newcastle three weeks ago; each-way shout.

stable_tour.quote: I think he can win a race or two before the end of the year as he's going the right way. He handles ease in the ground and stays well over a fast-run 6f, while a sharp 7f wouldn't bother him either. He's a bit of a stresshead who's hard on himself at home, but when he's on a going day he can be competitive. He looked unlucky at York two starts ago when he flew home on ground he didn't like. He's ready to start winning again and Ayr's big meeting could be in the pipeline for him. 07-08-25

runners.comment: Infrequent winner but on handy mark and should be sharper with a recent run behind him
runners.spotlight: Just one win to his name after 13 starts but he ended his 3yo campaign with two fine efforts, notably when chasing home a well-backed sprinter at Haydock in September (6f, good to soft; traffic problems at a crucial stage), and his return to action at Kempton should have blown away any cobwebs; best efforts on flat tracks but he is feasibly weighted if the undulations of Ripon aren't an issue.

runners.breeder: D & S L Tanker Transport Ltd
runners.comment: Made all in big C&D handicap last year off 3lb higher; good efffort latest; can't dismiss
runners.spotlight: Prolific winner down the year and although most of that success has come on AW, he did pick up a big pot on turf when making all in the Great St Wilfrid over C&D last August; ran well from a wide draw at Lingfield on Good Friday; on a dangerous mark but a central draw probably not ideal today.

quotes.race: William Hill/MND Association Great St Wilfrid Handicap
quotes.quote: It's a massive pot for a horse like Intervention. It's a big handicap for whatever horse it is, but at his age, he's just been an absolute star for us. We kind of felt he could run well, looking at the quality of the race this year. Outside the top three, it was a 0-90. With question marks against each of those three classier horses, we did feel that we had a decent chance and that the track would suit him - and it did. He wasn't much higher for Wolverhampton and he'd got good form on the all-weather off slightly higher marks. Martin [Dixon, brother and part-owner] got William [Pyle] booked very early on and his three pounds off was always going to help. We thought we were going to need a lightweight rider, so we thought we may as well take a little bit of weight off on top of that. William does seem one of those riders where some of these sprinters will just run for him - Chris Dixon, part-owner.

quotes.race: Win £2,000,000 With BetMGM's Golden Goals Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a fantastic win again and Intervention is just an amazing horse. That's eleven wins since we bought him, his last four on the bounce. He's going on seven, in the form of his life and is better than ever. It secures at least sharing the top prize for the all-weather horse of the month at the Arc (Arena Racing Company) tracks in December because that's three wins from his last three runs. We're thrilled with him, he came to us as a longstanding maiden and Mick's just worked wonders with him. He's a bit of a hero of ours, he's won more races for us than any other horse and he's a firm favourite - Chris Dixon, syndicate boss.

stable_tour.quote: Our winningmost horse with 11 victories. He had quite a few goes before we bought him and he's won all those races for us and well over £100,000 in prize-money. He's just a legend. He runs his race nearly every time and always seems to be in the money. He's come down to a good mark again for the all-weather season and he's ready to win again soon. He's having a break now and usually thrives through the winter. 26-09-24

runners.comment: On a dangerous mark and both runs for new yard have been encouraging enough; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Failed to win in 2025 but he has edged down the weights and his two AW runs for Paul Midgley have both been encouraging enough; no issue with the return to turf; type to win races sooner rather than later.

runners.comment: Good C&D form in a productive 2025 campaign; has gone well fresh; one to take seriously
runners.spotlight: Made a flying start to his 2025 campaign, his win in a C&D handicap last May completing a hat-trick; added another C&D handicap in August and also ran a fine race in a Class 2 here in September (off this mark); that C&D form makes him an interesting candidate for a stable with two wins in the race since 2019.

runners.comment: Did well last year, including over C&D; on a handy mark but his reappearance was low key
runners.spotlight: Prominent-racer; did well for this yard last year, winning at Thirsk in May and running several good races in defeat, notably when best of the stands' rail group in the Great St Wilfrid over C&D; he needs to leave his low-key seasonal return well behind if he is to feature today though.

quotes.race: Josh Mullins Rules Supreme Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Kodiac Thriller had been running over seven furlongs and a mile before we got him but he's been quick at home. I was quite pleased with him at Pontefract, I thought he needed it. He looked really comfortable today, he's very straightforward - Mark Walford, trainer.

runners.comment: Front-runner; shone in 2025 and last week's return to action was a good one; contender
runners.spotlight: Enthusiastic front-runner who shone for Ruth Carr in 2025, winning five 6f handicaps; fully effective over C&D and he made an encouraging seasonal return at Catterick last week, second of nine having been headed inside the final furlong (6f, good); looks the likeliest leader up the far side if the field split.

stable_tour.quote: He's a front-runner who wears his heart on his sleeve. He's really straightforward and a pleasure to have at the yard. He was a good second at Catterick on his reappearance last week. He's declared at Ripon on Thursday and we'll see what the handicapper does about the Catterick run. I don't really like to back them up too quickly on the back of a break, but he might run if the handicapper forces me to and he seems okay. 15-04-26

runners.breeder: D Ryan, D S Ryan & R A Williams

prev_owners.owner: C Barclay, Racing Knights & C Cleevely

runners.comment: Record in this race reads 1413; drying ground not ideal but can't rule out at this venue
runners.spotlight: Veteran who has been a regular in this event, winning in 2022 (soft) and 2024 (heavy) and hitting the frame in both 2023 and 2025; ended 2025 campaign with a pair of AW wins but he hasn't been at that level in either run this year; drying ground not ideal but he can never be ruled out completely at this track.

quotes.race: Wilmot-Smith Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: Fortamour broke well and I got a good position; everything just went so smoothly. He was pulling up as soon as he hit the front, but just seems to love this track - Paul Mulrennan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: 15th time lucky when winning a C&D maiden last June; absent since; returns in a warm race
runners.spotlight: Belatedly off the mark in a C&D maiden last June, his second run for Tim Easterby; more to do back in a competitive handicap after 302 days on the sidelines.

runners.comment: Losing run of 20 has seen him drop down the weights; yet to run well in four visits here
runners.spotlight: Hold-up sprinter and on a losing run of 20; well handicapped as a consequence and should be winning soon; whether it will be today, after 166 days off and at a track where he is yet to run well, is debatable.

runners.owner: Mps Racing, D Shapiro & D Clifford
runners.comment: Ended 2025 with a win but that was under ideal conditions, namely 5f and slow ground
runners.spotlight: Most of his racing in recent seasons has been at 5f and it was over that trip that he ended a losing streak at Musselburgh in November (soft); 6lb rise unlikely to prove beyond him under his optimum conditions (5f on slow ground) but others appeal more in this field.

prev_owners.owner: J Glover R O'Donnell J Short N Skinner

runners.comment: On a dangerous mark but there were more bad days than good in 2025; yet to shine here
runners.spotlight: More modest runs than good ones in 2025 but he did bolt up at Doncaster last June (6f, good to firm) and he is 4lb lower now; needs to leave his reappearance effort well behind him and he has finished down the field in his two visits here.

quotes.race: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap
quotes.quote: They probably went a gallop and then stopped as Another Investment stayed on. He's always had an engine and he's been a bit unlucky - Nigel Tinkler, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A very nice horse who'll be out again soon and will continue on to the all-weather. On his day he's very good but he needs everything to fall right. He only comes right at certain times - he's a bit moody. The faster the pace the better over 6f as he really wants 7f, but they rarely go the speed he wants in those races. 01-10-25

runners.comment: C&D winner; struggled for much of 2025; returns to action in a deep race
runners.spotlight: Won two of his first three starts, including a C&D nursery off 8lb higher, but the handicapper was in command for much of 2025; creditable third to Fortamour at Newcastle when last seen 145 days ago but he has more on his plate in this deeper race.

quotes.race: Paula Budge Surprise Birthday Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Lesley's Boy did well to win because he didn't really handle the track. I was off the bridle for most of the way, it was probably his ability that got him through today. It's a hard track, there are plenty of undulations but it worked out okay for me. He's improving with racing and I hope he keeps going the right way - Oisin Orr, jockey.

racecards.verdict: With his reappearance behind him, the unexposed SIXTYGEESBABY (nap) can take a step forward and record a first win for new connections.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/2 Sixtygeesbaby, 6/1 Wild Clary, 7/1 Kats Bob, 8/1 American Style, 9/1 Roberto Caro, 10/1 Almarada Prince,  Wen Moon, 12/1 Fortamour,  Modern Times, 14/1 Intervention, 16/1 Mister Sox,  Rock Opera,  Lesley's Boy, 20/1 It Just Takes Time, 33/1 Kodiac Thriller, 40/1 Another Investment

runners.comment: Three wins last year and he might be the type to continue to progress this season
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who won on handicap debut at Redcar (1m2f, good to soft) last May and scored twice in a row at Pontefract (1m2f good/good to firm) last summer; unplaced on final run last year and has to prove his current mark is within range, but he might be the type to continue to progress this season.

runners.comment: Five wins last year (two C&D); respectable reappearance; could show benefit of that run
runners.spotlight: Five wins last year (various ground), two of them over C&D, and campaign concluded with good third at Redcar in November; respectable reappearance run at Doncaster recently and could show the benefit of that outing today.

runners.comment: Twice well beaten last November but has had a break since; of interest on earlier form
runners.spotlight: Well beaten in Listed race and AW handicap on final two runs in November; however, a break may have helped and she's of interest judged on her two efforts last summer (1m1f/8.3f), when shaping as though 1m2f would suit.

runners.comment: Lightly raced 5yo who was a promising fourth on recent stable debut; on the shortlist
runners.spotlight: Failed to progress for Dermot Weld but this lightly raced 5yo was a promising fourth at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) on his recent stable and seasonal debut; could have more to offer for this yard; on the shortlist.

quotes.race: Buy Tickets At CorkRacecourse.ie Maiden
quotes.quote: Spoken Truth is a gorgeous big horse and wants better ground. A race like the Gallinule Stakes is a logical next step for him. I love the way he came home in the last furlong. He has a lot of talent - Dermot Weld, trainer.

runners.comment: Prolific last year after moving into handicaps; no surprise to see a bold bid on return
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who won her first five handicaps (8.6f/1m2f) last May/June and campaign concluded with close second of three to a progressive filly at Hamilton (1m1f) in August; no surprise to see a bold bid on her return, provided conditions suit (unproven on slow ground).

quotes.race: Dragonbet - Oncourse And Online Handicap
quotes.quote: Pomme Pomme didn't know what she was doing when she started but she's certainly got the hang of it now. We knew she had a great chance and she's seen the mile and a quarter out well again, plus I always thought she'd be better on this type of ground. She's bombproof and we know the family well as Dad trained the dam [Apple Anni]. We'll see what the handicapper does and then we'll go again - Jack Channon, trainer.

runners.owner: S Bulmer, P Hebdon & R Taylor
runners.comment: 0-11 last year but runner-up three times, including in this race on his reappearance
runners.spotlight: 0-11 last year when not at his best on his final few runs; however, he was runner-up three times last season, including in this race on his reappearance (good), and he's 2lb lower 12 months on; capable of having a big say.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice colt by Cracksman who's had only one run, finishing fifth at York. We like him and you'd think he'll be a middle-distance horse. 23-04-24

runners.breeder: Epona Bloodstock Ltd And P A Byrne
runners.comment: 0-10 last year but placed a few times, including on last two starts last autumn
runners.spotlight: 0-10 last year but runner-up on his reappearance last April (1m, good) and placed off today's mark on his final two outings last autumn (1m2f, good to soft/soft); might not be far away on this return to action.

quotes.race: Racehorse Lotto Handicap
quotes.quote: We've always thought a lot of Austrian Theory and he was a very talented two-year-old. I thought he was a real Golden Mile type for Goodwood last year but he can be a bit in and out. His run at Chester last weekend was a sign he was coming back to the boil and Joe Fanning was sublime on the front end. The straight track handicaps don't really suit him and, albeit the plan didn't come off last year, we'll be working back from the Golden Mile again - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a grand horse who we bought from the Horses In Training Sale in Newmarket. He's not quite ready to run yet, but we're looking forward to him this summer. I'm still learning about him, but I'd expect him to want a mile and good ground and to be running at some of the bigger meetings. 23-04-24

prev_owners.owner: Middleham Park Racing Lxvii And Partner

runners.comment: Below best on AW this year and has to raise his game now back on turf
runners.spotlight: Has race-fitness on his side and his reduced mark appeals on last spring's AW wins; however, he hasn't been at the same level across his five AW starts this year and has to raise his game now back on turf.

stable_tour.quote: A fairly well-handicapped horse with plenty of ability who has grown and is beginning to look the part. He won for the first time at Chelmsford on Friday and seems to be going the right way. He could get further than a mile and there are plenty more races to be won with him. 22-04-25

runners.comment: Underwhelming on stable debut but may have needed the run; progressive last season
runners.spotlight: Underwhelming fifth of six on last month's stable and seasonal debut at Southwell (1m3f, AW), but he was wide early and may have needed the run; progressive on turf last season for William Haggas and he could tap back into that promise and play a leading role today.

runners.comment: On a handy mark on last August's form & could be a contender for last year's winning yard
runners.spotlight: Down the field on final two runs last season but he may have been ready for a break; on a handy mark based on his form last August and could be a contender for last year's winning yard.

racecards.verdict: The ex-Irish SPOKEN TRUTH made an encouraging start for David O'Meara when fourth at Doncaster last month and earns the vote.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Spoken Truth, 13/2 Austrian Theory,  Sir William, 7/1 Pomme Pomme, 8/1 Spioradalta, 9/1 Financer, 10/1 Cristo, 11/1 Raulin, 14/1 Lunar Eclipse,  Glistening Nights

racecards.race_name: Racing BetBuilder At Spreadex Sports Handicap

runners.owner: A Scaife, C Scaife, G Scaife
runners.comment: The step up in trip is worth a go on stable debut and he's one to consider
runners.spotlight: All five runs for Clive Cox on AW, going close in four-runner handicap at Kempton (7f) last month; sold for 24,000gns since; has shaped as though this step up to 1m is worth a go; one to consider on stable/turf debut.

runners.owner: E Holmes, M Graham And P Day

prev_owners.owner: E Holmes, M Graham And Partner

runners.comment: Second on debut last September; two lesser runs followed but not ruled out on h'cap debut
runners.spotlight: Kept on for second on debut at Carlisle (6f, soft) last September; two lesser runs followed (6f/1m, AW/good) but she retains potential in view of that initial promise, and she's not ruled out on handicap/seasonal debut.

runners.owner: D Bishop, S Bland & T Coyle
runners.comment: Just one good run among his four 2yo starts but attractive mark on that York effort
runners.spotlight: Down the field on three of his four 2yo starts, most recently on handicap debut at Beverley (8.4f, soft) in September when last seen; however, he's had wind surgery since and is on an attractive mark judged on his sixth of 16 at York (7f, good) last July; could be a contender.

runners.comment: Failed to threaten across his four 2yo starts; has to raise his game on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Well-bred sort but he failed to threaten on his three 2yo starts for Clive Cox, the latest his handicap debut at Nottingham (1m, good) in October; sold for 16,000gns later that month; has to raise his game on stable debut.

runners.comment: 0-6 but has shown promise and the first-time hood could help him settle better; chance
runners.spotlight: 0-6 but has twice finished runner-up (including on turf) and he was denied a clear run when sixth of nine, beaten only about 2l, at Newcastle (1m, AW) last time; the first-time hood could help him settle better; chance.

runners.comment: Remains a maiden after nine starts but placed a few times, including last month (1m, AW)
runners.spotlight: Remains a maiden after nine starts but he's been runner-up in two handicaps (including on turf) and was a close third at Newcastle (1m, AW) most recently; every chance he'll be thereabouts once more.

runners.comment: Comfortable win on AW when last seen; player if continuing the good work back on turf
runners.spotlight: He got better with each of his three runs in nurseries last autumn, winning comfortably at Newcastle (1m, AW) in November; gelded since; he needs to transfer his improvement back to turf but is bred to do better still and a 6lb rise might not stop him if he can continue the good work.

runners.comment: Won in good style at Newcastle then raced wide early when third at Southwell
runners.spotlight: All seven starts on AW; got off the mark at the sixth attempt in first-time cheekpieces (retained) at Newcastle (7f) last month, doing it comfortably from the front; third under a penalty at Southwell (7f) seven days later and now another 4lb higher, but he raced wide early last time and may yet to have more to offer in the headgear; chance if seeing out 1m.

runners.comment: Showed ability last year but improvement is needed if he's to make a winning stable debut
runners.spotlight: Displayed ability among his six (winless) 2yo starts for Des Donovan; sold for 7,750gns last October and gelded since; however, improvement is needed in first-time cheekpieces if he's to make a winning stable debut.

runners.comment: Half-brother to four winners who goes handicapping off a basement mark for in-form yard
runners.spotlight: He didn't show much in the winter on his first three starts (7f/1m, AW); however, this half-brother to four winners goes handicapping off a basement mark for his in-form yard and is a possible improver; interesting, all the more so if attracting market support.

runners.breeder: Floors Stud Ltd & The Duke Of Devonshire
runners.comment: 0-7 last year but went close the only time he wore these blinkers; gelded since last start
runners.spotlight: 0-7 last year but the only time he wore these blinkers he was beaten just a neck at Redcar (1m, good to soft) in September; gelded since his last run in November; no surprise if he has a part to play on reappearance.

racecards.verdict: Tony Coyle and Kaine Wood's horses are running well and the reappearing SINGARDA is on a good mark judged on his best 2yo performance.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Saxon Prince, 9/2 Ciao Capo, 5/1 Norcross Brow,  Sailor Batt, 6/1 Fickle McSelfish, 12/1 Singarda,  Domination, 14/1 Gwen's Girl,  Walk On Walk On, 16/1 Leysthorpe Star, 25/1 Hood Wink

racecards.race_name: Go Racing In Yorkshire Apprentice Handicap (Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Series)

runners.comment: 3-3 last year prior to October heavy-ground defeat; could still have more left in the tank
runners.spotlight: Made it 3-3 for the year (1m, good/soft) when winning at Ascot last September; well beaten at Doncaster in October but on heavy ground; this is his first run since and he could still have more left in the tank.

quotes.race: LK Bennett Lady Amateur Jockeys Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys)
quotes.quote: Walsingham jumped really well and took a strong hold, Danny Tudhope said he can race lazily but he didn't today. He travelled into it really well, but I could have done with something taking me into the race a bit longer because when he hit the front he didn't do too much. He's done it nicely. I know it's hard to get home here at Ascot on soft ground, so I was keeping an eye on the leaders but he was always giving me such a good feel that I knew I'd get them back - Brodie Hampson, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: We paid 50,000gns for him around this time last year but he hasn't run for us yet. He was working very well in the spring and then had a little setback just as he was ready to run. He had some strong maiden form in Ireland when he was trained by Dermot Weld and he's definitely well handicapped. He runs at Redcar on Wednesday and it might take him a run or two to get back after his long time off. He'd be one to follow as I'm pretty sure there's mileage in his mark. 26-09-24

runners.comment: Two wins last year and may have needed reappearance outing in the Spring Mile
runners.spotlight: Two wins last year (1m/1m1f, good/soft); the last of them came in a seller and he was well beaten on last month's reappearance at Doncaster, but that was the competitive Spring Mile and he may have needed the run; won this in 2022 and he's not discounted off a handy mark.

quotes.race: William Hill Top Price Guarantee Autumn Handicap
quotes.quote: We were getting Empirestateofmind ready for the Lincoln when he injured a hock and that put him on the back foot. We thought he'd run well in the Cambridgeshire but he was drawn in the middle and he was a bit fresh. He always needs a run. It's good to get him back. He's in the Balmoral Handicap next week and he'll run if he gets in - John Quinn, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Summer Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: Empirestateofmind bumped into one at Newcastle last Saturday and he deserved that, he's so consistent. This is a very nice race to win - Ross Harmon, owner.

stable_tour.quote: Unfortunately he won't be able to run in the Lincoln, which he finished seventh in last year, as he needed three weeks of rest at just the wrong time. He could be out in May and he's a good handicapper when the ground gets soft. He's been a victim of his consistency over the last 18 months as his mark didn't come down even though he didn't win, but he starts now lower than he did last year and I don't imagine he's any worse, so I hope he can win a nice handicap at some stage. 20-03-24

runners.owner: Rise One Racing And W A Bethell
runners.comment: Won three times last year and could leave his reappearance performance miles behind
runners.spotlight: Tailed off on last month's reappearance in the Spring Mile at Doncaster but may have needed the run and those ridden more patiently came to the fore; he won three times last year (1m1f/1m, soft/good) and it will be no surprise if he leaves that latest performance miles behind.

stable_tour.quote: He has run seven times this season, with two wins and five places, so he's been remarkably consistent. We got him leased by his owner-breeder. The Rise One Partnership took one half of him and we've got the other half. He'll go to the sales at the end of the season. Regarding ground, he won in bottomless conditions at Carlisle in July, with my stable girl Hannah Dring on board. So he clearly goes on heavy but, saying that, before the race I was saying “Can we just pull him out?” It was good ground when he won at Carlisle last time. He'll have a couple more runs before the end of the season and has been declared to run at Pontefract on Thursday. 17-09-25

runners.comment: Well handicapped on turf form last April/June but hasn't shone on AW this year
runners.spotlight: Dead-heated over C&D (good) last April and went very close at Carlisle in June; well handicapped on that form but a long way below his best on AW this year; the return to turf needs to trigger a major revival.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Global Stallions Handicap
quotes.quote: We were up 11lb in a better grade on totally different ground so we went with an open mind again and Good Morning Alex has done it well. He's been a real surprise package from going to the all-weather in December thinking it was a last-chance saloon. He's just grown up and matured. In fairness, he was a late foal but he's improved out of all recognition. Connor [Beasley, jockey] said he wouldn't want the ground any faster than it was today so I think a lot will depend on the weather as to where we go. This was very much the target - Nicola Barron, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Second in this last year and reappeared with promising fifth at Doncaster; in the mix
runners.spotlight: The vast majority of his wins have come on slow ground but the going was good when he was second in this race last year; reappeared with promising fifth of 22 in the Spring Mile at Doncaster and could be in the mix.

quotes.race: AGMA 20 Years Of Franklin Ownership Carlisle Bell Handicap
quotes.quote: On The River had slightly lost his way but he won well. We had to run because he needs soft ground. There's a ladies' race we might come back here for - William Bethell. owner and assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Yorkshire Wonder Horse Race Is On Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: On The River won on this day last year. He's consistent. I was a bit worried about the ground over this trip but he toughed it out. He's got a good attitude - Ben Haslam, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's an absolute star, a real dude. I've won with him nine times. A bit like Yanifer, you can't really get horses above the age of four who improve, but they both have. He was rated 63 the first time I won with him and he won the Carlisle Bell off a mark 80 in June. I remember when we first had him and he won three, I thought “Oh God, we aren't going to win any with him next season.” Then he won four the next year. There's a chance he'll go to Ayr with Yanifer or go for a Chester seller, which sounds brutal but I don't think anyone will bid £40,000 for him. He's just a little weed with a heart the size of a dustbin lid. 17-09-25

runners.comment: Won at Newcastle last October but in blinkers, not the cheekpieces he wears today
runners.spotlight: In good form in blinkers towards the end of last year, winning at Newcastle (1m, AW) in October; however, he has a poor strike-rate and wasn't at his best in cheekpieces at Newcastle (1m, AW) three weeks ago following a break; cheekpieces remain on today.

stable_tour.quote: He's £1,500 very well spent as he's earned nearly £32,000 for us. He's a funny horse with loads of talent and, although he's only won once, he's kept bringing in good prize-money, so I accept it. You have to humour him and do things on his terms - I think he nearly shocked himself when he won at Newcastle this month. 29-10-25

runners.comment: 11yo; below par at the end of last season but ran well in this on his comeback last April
runners.spotlight: 11yo who was below par at the end of last season but reappeared last April with a good fourth in this race (good) and picked up three wins subsequently; he's 3lb below his last winning mark and is not ruled out.

quotes.race: Bishopton Equine Handicap
quotes.quote: Garden Oasis was quickly away and I needed that as I knew there was going to be more pace in the race and, obviously drawn one, I could hold the rail if I was quick out so it was ideal, but I did have to go a little bit quicker than I wanted to into the bend. I got a bit of a breather round it but he does stay a bit further so you can stretch them and make sure they don't come past you at any speed. He's as game as they come and loves it around here - David Allan, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 519 Handicap
quotes.quote: Garden Oasis is still full of enthusiasm. You've got to run the speed off them as he's getting older and he's not got the turn of foot he used to have but he digs in really well for you - David Allan, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Visit attheraces.com Handicap
quotes.quote: Garden Oasis absolutely thrives around this place, and the most important thing was just to jump from the gates fast. He was soon on the front end and dug in well - David Allen, rider

quotes.race: Visit attheraces.com Handicap
quotes.quote: I'd love a yard full of horses like Garden Oasis, he's wonderful. He's very uncomplicated, the more you complicate it the worse he runs. He's tough, he likes it here and he goes on pretty much any ground - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Visit attheraces.com Handicap
quotes.quote: Every time Garden Oasis ran last season he came back not right. He was actually in the sales but we decided not to sell him. It took a long time to get him right in the winter but he's been sound and okay recently and ran a good race at Haydock but just didn't get home. David won it in the first furlong - Tim Easterby, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a bit disappointingly at Ripon, where he just didn't fire for some reason, but he's come out of that well. A mile is his trip, on good ground. 02-05-22

runners.comment: Three wins last May/July & is on last winning mark; may improve for this reappearance run
runners.spotlight: Three wins last May/July at about 1m on various ground and he's back down to his last winning mark; may have been ready for a break towards end of last season but there's a suspicion he'll improve for this comeback run.

runners.comment: Runner-up five times last May-August but went off the boil in the autumn; reappearance
runners.spotlight: Runner-up five times last May-August and he's on an attractive mark on that form; however, he went off the boil in the autumn and his long losing run continues; needs to get back on track on this reappearance.

quotes.race: Jeffrey King Memorial Race Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Barley probably needed the run at Doncaster, not from a fitness point of view but to wake him up as he's very laid-back. We got a really soft lead today and were able to dictate. He's a lovely-looking horse and has a good attitude. He'll stay further and be better in a better race, where I think he'd be able to show his full potential - Rob Hornby, jockey.

runners.owner: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
runners.comment: Needs to build on last month's comeback at Southwell and the blinkers are left off
runners.spotlight: Won off this mark in first-time blinkers at York (7f, good) last July and he could improve for last month's respectable comeback at Southwell (7f, AW); however, he does need to build on that and blinkers are left off.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Extra Places Every Day Handicap
quotes.quote: Oli Stammers does plenty of work with us at home and he suggested the blinkers and coming back in trip. It worked! We always thought Chesneys Charm wanted a bit of a trip and it could be that a mile will be best for him -  Grant Tuer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a good campaign. It's been very tricky working out his trip, but we pulled him back to 7f at York and put some blinkers on and he won. The race worked out well for him and he's taken advantage of it. He ran well at Southwell last week in a really good race for the grade over a mile and we'll come back to 7f next time. Soft ground is going to suit him and the plan is to go to Carlisle next week and then a race at Ayr on Gold Cup day. 04-09-25

racecards.verdict: Last year's runner-up ON THE RIVER ran well when fifth of 22 in the Spring Mile at Doncaster on his reappearance and gets the nod.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 On The River, 9/2 Walsingham, 7/1 Barley, 8/1 Mr Mistoffelees,  Chesneys Charm, 9/1 Garden Oasis,  Cosmos Raj, 10/1 Empirestateofmind,  Milteye, 16/1 Good Morning Alex

runners.comment: Ballyburn's half-sister too keen, soundly beaten in Fairyhouse bumper; switches to hurdles
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to seven winners, notably same yard's high-class bumper winner and 2m-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Ballyburn; cost 92,000euros as a 3yo; too keen, soundly beaten on debut in Fairyhouse fillies' bumper in December; switches to hurdles now.

runners.comment: Mildly encouraging recent hurdles debut; more needed and more fluency needed in jumping
runners.spotlight: Failed to land a blow on debut at Thurles in December; more encouraging hurdles debut this month, staying on late after some novicey jumping when remote fourth in 2m3f Cork mares' maiden (yielding); more needed.

runners.comment: Remote last early this month in Cork hunters chase (keen, mistakes); switches to hurdles
runners.spotlight: Placed in her two point-to-points last month, remote last of four on rules debut early this month in Cork maiden hunters chase (keen, mistakes); switches to hurdles and best watched.

runners.comment: Initial promise in maiden hurdles but hasn't progressed; looking exposed
runners.spotlight: Initial promise in maiden hurdles but hasn't progressed, well held on handicap debut last month; looking exposed but can't be ruled out in an ordinary maiden.

runners.comment: Behind throughout here last month in bumper; can only be watched now switched to hurdles
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to four winners inc Isabella Bee (2m-2m3f hurdle/chase), Diamond Koda (2m3f hurdle) and Fleur De La Roque (French 2m1f hurdle); dam useful 1m4f Flat/2m1f hurdle winner; 80-1, behind throughout on debut here last month in fillies' bumper; can only be watched now switched to hurdles.

runners.comment: Staying on second in 2m4f Navan maiden last month; leading claims in an ordinary maiden
runners.spotlight: Decent efforts in maiden hurdles, notably place claims when unseating at the last over this trip at Leopardstown and most recently staying on second in 2m4f Navan maiden last month (soft); return to this trip to suit and leading claims in an ordinary maiden.

runners.comment: Four bumper efforts have amounted to little and well held in Rathcannon point' 4 days ago
runners.spotlight: Four bumper efforts have amounted to little and well held in Rathcannon point-to-point four days ago; can only be watched on hurdles debut.

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras D'Enkie
runners.comment: Lame on debut in bumper a while ago; respected if strong in the market on hurdles debut
runners.spotlight: 160,000euros 3yo; half-sister to four winners inc Yala Enki (high-class 2m1f-3m4f hurdle/chase); dam French maiden jumper; second favourite, reportedly lame when soundly beaten on debut in good-class 2m3f Punchestown mares' bumper in December 2024; respected if strong in the market on hurdles debut.

runners.owner: Emma Sheahan & E Fox & E Sheahan
runners.comment: Pulled up in sole point; market likely best guide on rules debut
runners.spotlight: Sister to a bumper winner and from the family of smart staying chaser Tullymurry Toff; not without market support but pulled up in a Bartlemy point-to-point in May last year; market likely best guide on rules debut.

runners.breeder: G Durrheim And Maria Mulcahy Durrheim
runners.comment: Never sighted on last month's debut in Cork bumper; best watched now switched to hurdles
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to bumper and useful 2m-2m5f hurdle/chase winner A Different Kind; 28-1, never sighted on last month's debut in Cork bumper; best watched now switched to hurdles.

runners.comment: Debut promise last month over 2m; likely improver upped in trip and one to consider
runners.spotlight: Third foal; dam bumper/2m4f hurdle winner, sister to 3m1f chase winner Kalabaloo; 20-1, promising debut in 2m Gowran mares' maiden last month, staying-on third of 10 behind an odds-on shot (heavy); step up in trip here could suit and could well improve enough to feature.

runners.comment: Never sighted (tailed off) on recent debut in 2m1f Cork maiden; can only be watched
runners.spotlight: Ocovango filly; dam point winner/third in bumper, half-sister to 2m hurdle winner Shanroe Society; never sighted (tailed off) on recent debut in 2m1f Cork maiden; can only be watched for now.

runners.comment: Chased home a ready winner here last month (soft); tries a longer trip
runners.spotlight: Fair Flat maiden in Britain for James Horton; shaped okay on all three maiden hurdle runs over 2m, notably latest when (favourite) chasing home a ready winner here last month (soft); tries a longer trip here.

racecards.verdict: It may to side with the more experienced FLY AWAY HOME, a staying-on second over 2m4f last time and should appreciate this longer trip
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Babyburn, 3/1 Fly Away Home, 7/2 Kisuton Enki, 13/2 Meghan Mala, 8/1 Louie's Folly, 9/1 Doing It In Style, 12/1 Little Neck Road, 16/1 Chosen Princess, 50/1 Dream Frequency,  Ma Lumiere, 66/1 Dceilingcantholdus,  Jessie Roe,  Breeze Of Tobruk

runners.comment: Point/hurdles winner; Galway second reads well; not beaten far on handicap debut; player
runners.spotlight: Point winner; 0-4 in bumpers; improved for a tongue-tie over hurdles until dropping out very tamely in Navan Grade 3; the form of his second at Galway reads well; not beaten far on handicap debut at Leopardstown; hard to dismiss.

quotes.race: Gowran Park Racing Club Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: We always liked Ma Jacks Hill at home but he was disappointing in bumpers. He got his wind done and that probably brought out improvement in him. He'll be a nicer horse on nicer ground as well. He's a fine, big galloping horse, so hopefully it's onwards and upwards - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He had a wind op before he won at Gowran and it seems to have worked well. He's a gorgeous-looking horse and bumped into a nice type at Galway on Sunday. He stuck at it well enough and hopefully there is more to come from him. He's a chaser down the line and you won't see the best of him until he sees a fence. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Trip-versatile and enjoys the mud; went close twice in December, including around here
runners.spotlight: Won Navan handicap hurdle (2m4f, soft) in January of last year off 102 before following up in Fairyhouse novice (2m, heavy); moderate seasonal return at Punchestown but pair of runner-up finishes followed at 2m4f/3m; fair fourth at Naas (15.5f) on latest; solid chance in first-time blinkers.

runners.comment: Last year's winner off 1lb lower; poor chasing this season; not discounted back hurdling
runners.spotlight: Last year's winner off 1lb lower but hasn't won since; below his best chasing this season, albeit set some stiff tasks; not discounted back hurdling but veteran will need to improve significantly.

quotes.race: "Bet Through The Free Racing Post App" Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Grange Walk is a fair horse who is only coming to himself. He'll probably go on for the Dan Moore at Fairyhouse from here. I was very happy coming here - I couldn't believe that Danny Mullins went to Kempton [to ride Tornado Flyer in the King George]. This horse is only a six-year-old so time is on his side - John Ryan, trainer.

quotes.race: Frank O'Beirne Memorial Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Grange Walk is a proper one and I think he would have won at Galway but for falling. Bryan (Cooper) said he won with something in hand. He's only six and the sky is the limit for him. He'll be a novice chaser, not a handicapper - John Ryan, trainer.

quotes.race: Adare Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Grange Walk is going to be a smashing chaser. He's very scopey and Danny (Mullins) has loved him from the first time he schooled him.  He actually turned to me then and said we have a Draycott Place or Kylecrue back again in terms of the way this lad jumps. He'll probably go for the two miles and two furlongs in Galway next. Two miles is his trip but he gets that distance no problem on good ground - John Ryan, trainer.

quotes.race: Doneraile Walk Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Danny gave Grange Walk a peach of a ride today, I thought he was absolutely brilliant. We were short a little bit of fitness so we held him up a bit. He'll go to Listowel now for a novice or a handicap. He probably wasn't ready for the novice in Galway and the hill probably caught him a bit. He is a good horse and can go wherever he likes - John Ryam, trainer

runners.comment: Some good hurdles form; best form is on a sounder surface and might need the run
runners.spotlight: Gained second hurdles win at Clonmel (19.5f, good) last May off 101; went close there the following month when 1.25l fourth; was last seen finishing second at Clonmel again in October; best form is on a sounder surface and might need the run.

runners.comment: Seven-time winner and hasn't been out of the first 3 in his last six starts around here
runners.spotlight: Seven-time winner over hurdles/fences and hasn't been out of the first three in his last six starts around here; three wins over fences last year; disappointing favourite over hurdles at Cork but returns from a break racing from 14lb lower hurdles mark; should go well.

quotes.race: Wexford Racecourse Supporters Club Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Crowsatedeappletart has got a mind of his own, he likes things happening quickly to keep him interested. Jumping off, dropping back to two miles caught him on the backfoot but the good jumps over the first few kept him in a nice position. I had a nice bit of room down the inner. He is such a tough horse; it is like he is coming into his prime now. I got checked turning in, got run out of room and he still battled back all the way up the run-in. I rode him in Cork and it was borderline soft over two and half miles and I thought he wanted every inch of it, so for Mick [Winters, trainer] to sharpen him up for that today over two miles on better ground than he has been running on was a good performance - Gavin Brouder, jockey.

quotes.race: Molloy Metal Recycling Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Crowsatedappletart got a 7lb pull with May Call You Back to reserve the form. Some horses improve by having more runs. He did that before when he went to Cork and followed up the next week with a good run in Limerick. He is a funny horse and he has tracks that he likes. We were here early before racing and he was fierce happy asleep in the stable. We may come back here in a couple of weeks - Michael Winters, trainer.

runners.comment: Ballinrobe winner for Gordon Elliott; off the track 901 days; new yard; best watched
runners.spotlight: Won Ballinrobe maiden hurdle for Gordon Elliott on debut in April 2023 but not seen since down the field in Galway handicap 901 days ago; first run for new yard; best watched.

stable_tour.quote: He's a low-grade handicap hurdler but the guys who own him should have plenty of fun with him. He'll win races. 24-10-23

runners.owner: Mrs T Hyde & Mrs Paul Shanahan
runners.comment: Ballinrobe maiden winner last season (2m1f, good); struggled over 2m4f since; prefers good
runners.spotlight: Ballinrobe maiden winner last season (2m1f, good); well held twice since over around 2m4f, latest after winter break in Gowran handicap in February on heavy; ground looks against her here.

runners.comment: Course winner won over fences at Cork in January; fell six out here over fences on latest
runners.spotlight: Won course maiden hurdle in 2024; got off the mark over fences in Cork beginners' in January in first-time headgear combination; still in with a shout when unseating rider six out in handicap chase here 16 days ago; conditions suitable; chance.

quotes.race: William Hill Each Way Extra Challenge Series Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Way Down South won his maiden hurdle last year, and we thought he would progress from that, but he didn't. He went backwards. He enjoys fences. He ran poorly at Limerick and it was a gamble bringing him back so quickly, but the cheekpieces helped, the tongue-tie helped, the ground helped, dropping him back two furlongs helped, and he jumped well. But Dan knows him, it takes a jockey to know him - Gillian Scott, trainer.

quotes.race: Cuchulainn Maiden Hurdle (In Memory Of Andrew McNamara)
quotes.quote: Way Down South can be quite hard on himself, so we said we'd jump him out in front and see how we get on. I'm delighted it worked out and he is a nice horse for the future - Gillian Scott, trainer.

racecards.verdict: Course specialist CROWSATEDAPPLETART gets the nod on his return, racing from a 14lb lower hurdles mark compared to his chase rating
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Crowsatedappletart, 4/1 Collaborative,  Colleen Danu, 5/1 Ma Jacks Hill, 13/2 Way Down South, 10/1 Grange Walk, 14/1 Jay Jay Zee, 20/1 Miss Corby

runners.comment: 150,000euros yearling; half-brother to top-class dual Champion Chase winner Altior
runners.spotlight: Mastercraftsman gelding; 150,000euros yearling; half-brother to dual Champion Chase winner Altior; dam bumper/2m1f hurdle winner; will need to be above-average to win this on debut but he might well be.

runners.comment: Never out of first three in six hurdles starts; will go well again but becoming costly
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner; useful form in six hurdling starts, never out of the first three; third of 21 in Listed DRF handicap in February (3m, heavy); runner-up in 2m4f Fairyhouse maiden hurdle 12 days ago; will go well again but is becoming costly to follow.

quotes.race: Skryne GAA Day Out At Navan Racecourse INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: He Can't Dance is a big galloper. He's better than that, they just didn't go much of a gallop. He will be a nice horse - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was disappointing at Galway on Sunday. He got very tired and we'll see how he comes out of the race before deciding where he goes next. I'd like to think he's a lot better than he showed there. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Classy form at Cheltenham before poor run here when odds-on; pulled up at the Festival
runners.spotlight: Point winner; only second run over hurdles when third behind No Drama This End (runner-up also a class act) in Cheltenham Grade 2 in November (2m5f, soft); defeated at odds-on in very testing conditions in course maiden; pulled up in the Albert Bartlet; rated 130 and one to beat.

stable_tour.quote: He's still a maiden but he could run well in the Albert Bartlett. He was behind No Drama This End at Cheltenham when he was still very green and then I thought it would have been softer at Limerick over Christmas. He's a really nice horse and he has a similar profile to Minella Indo heading for the race because he was also a maiden. 15-02-26

runners.comment: Hasn't fired since finishing second in Clonmel maiden hurdle in December; too much to find
runners.spotlight: Hasn't really fired since finishing second in Clonmel maiden hurdle in December; too much to find on ratings.

runners.comment: Refused on debut at Leopardstown; triple-figure odds and never a factor in 3 starts since
runners.spotlight: Refused at the second on debut at Leopardstown; triple-figure odds and never a factor in three starts since; look elsewhere.

runners.owner: John P Coleman & M J Caffrey
runners.comment: Modest maiden after eight starts and can't be fancied taking on far superior opposition
runners.spotlight: Modest maiden after eight starts and can't be fancied taking on far superior opposition.

runners.comment: Hinted at some ability but modest form all the same; likely to come up well short
runners.spotlight: Modest third in Gowran bumper (2m, soft to heavy) in January 2025; tailed off here after absence on hurdles debut in Februray; likely to fall well short.

runners.comment: Pulled up in pair of point-to-points; beaten out of sight in four hurdle starts
runners.spotlight: Pulled up in pair of point-to-points; beaten out of sight in four hurdle starts; safe to rule out.

racecards.verdict: The interesting one is CASUAL WATER, a half-brother to Altior making his debut for the champion trainer
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/10 King's Bucks, 5/2 Casual Water,  He Can't Dance, 18/1 Loyal Praetorian, 33/1 Tradonthebay, 66/1 Three County Star, 100/1 Sam's Favourite, 200/1 Strand Street Lass

runners.comment: Leopardstown maiden winner well held at Cheltenham twice since; drops in grade now
runners.spotlight: Hooded since looking tricky on his debut, showing decent turn of foot to win Leopardstown maiden at Christmas but soundly beaten both starts since in competitive Cheltenham contests, too keen and hung right first occasion and then never sighted in Fred Winter at the Festival; down in grade here.

quotes.race: Paddy Power I Have No Idea What Day It Is 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: We fancied Hardy Stuff in one of those Academy Hurdles early on and he ran out at the first bend. He'd a good run the last day when we dropped him in to get him settled and he flew home. They went a good gallop which suited him well and he came home strong. He could be one for the Fred Winter - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

runners.comment: Didn't count in Leopardstown mares' handicap at DRF; this less competitive
runners.spotlight: Off the mark in Down Royal maiden last summer (2m1f, good) and better form when second in 2m Gowran handicap on soft; after a break didn't count in very valuable Leopardstown mares' handicap at the DRF in February; this is less competitive so don't rule out.

runners.comment: C&D maiden run at Christmas encouraging; respected on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in Belclare maiden point-to-point and nice bit of improvement on second maiden hurdle run when C&D fifth (heavy) at Christmas; unable to build on that at Down Royal following month when fourth (second and third won afterwards) but still enters calculations on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Shock C&D winner last month should go well again despite 6lb rise
runners.spotlight: Killarney juvenile maiden hurdle winner last summer and returned from winter break for shock 25-1 win in C&D handicap last month (soft), patiently ridden and coming home well to win with a bit in hand; 6lb rise looks workable, should go well.

quotes.race: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I'm delighted with Something Noble and we were noticing in his work recently that while he isn't the quickest horse, if you hold him up, he has a bit of a gear. I told Eoghan to ride his own race, he gave him a lovely confident ride for a 7lb claimer. He'll go over fences soon as he can utilise his 4yo allowance and is a lovely big type. He is a Flat-bred but doesn't look like one, and has now won two hurdle races - Ciaran Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Killarney Park Hotel 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Something Noble had been going nicely at home, had three lovely runs on the Flat. Colin [Keane] got off him the last time and said if you want a 3yo hurdler this could be your one. He won't be one that we can rush as he is a big scopey lad but is a nice horse going forward - Ciaran Murphy, trainer, speaking to RacingTV.

runners.comment: Too keen at Gowran last time; tongue-tie back on and previous C&D winner; claims
runners.spotlight: C&D maiden hurdle winner (heavy) in November; has run well in a couple of handicaps although too keen and didn't get home on latest at Gowran; not one to rule out, providing he settles better (tongue-tie added).

runners.breeder: Miss L Cronin & Mrs U Lawler
